at vaccinere.explanation: "At vaccinere" means "to vaccinate". To name the disease, add "mod" (against): "vaccinere mod influenza" (vaccinate against the flu). To say you are the person getting the shot, use "at lade sig vaccinere" (to let yourself be vaccinated): "Jeg lader mig vaccinere" (I am getting vaccinated).

sentence.da: Lægen vil **vaccinere** alle børn i klassen mod mæslinger.
sentence.en: The doctor will vaccinate all the children in the class against measles.

at vade.explanation: "At vade" means "to wade". To say you walk out into the sea, add "ud i" (out into): "Vi vader ud i havet" (We wade out into the sea). To say someone is very rich, use "i penge" (in money): "Hun vader i penge" (She is rolling in money).

sentence.da: Vi kan **vade** over åen, fordi vandet ikke er dybt.
sentence.en: We can wade across the stream because the water is not deep.

at vakle.explanation: "At vakle" means "to wobble or waver". To say a tired person walks unsteadily, use it for "to wobble": "Han vakler hjem" (He wobbles home). To say a decision is not firm, use it for "to waver": "Hans beslutning vakler" (His decision is wavering).

sentence.da: Stolen vil **vakle**, fordi det ene ben er kortere.
sentence.en: The chair will wobble because one leg is shorter.

at vande.explanation: "At vande" means "to water". It comes from "vand" (water). To say you give animals water to drink, use it for them too: "at vande hestene" (to water the horses).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vande** blomsterne, fordi det ikke har regnet.
sentence.en: I have to water the flowers because it has not rained.

at vandre.explanation: "At vandre" means "to wander or hike". To say you go on foot for a long time in nature, use it for "to hike": "Vi vandrer langs kysten" (We hike along the coast). To say you walk around without hurry or goal, use it for "to wander": "Han vandrede rundt i byen" (He wandered around town).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vandre** fem timer i bjergene og sove i telt.
sentence.en: We want to hike five hours in the mountains and sleep in a tent.

at vare.explanation: "At vare" means "to last". To say how long something goes on, add the length of time: "Filmen varer to timer" (The movie lasts two hours).

sentence.da: Mødet vil **vare** i cirka en time.
sentence.en: The meeting will last about an hour.

at variere.explanation: "At variere" means "to vary". To say something is not always the same, use it alone: "Prisen varierer" (The price varies). To say you change something on purpose, name the thing after it: "Jeg varierer menuen" (I vary the menu).

sentence.da: Temperaturen kan **variere** meget fra dag til dag.
sentence.en: The temperature can vary a lot from day to day.

at vaske.explanation: "At vaske" means "to wash". To say you wash an object, name it after the verb: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car). To say you wash yourself, use "at vaske sig" (to wash oneself): "Jeg vasker mig" (I wash myself). To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vaske** tøjet i dag.
sentence.en: I want to wash the clothes today.

at vaske gulv.explanation: "At vaske gulv" means "to mop the floor". In this phrase, "gulv" has no article. For example, "Vi vasker gulv om lørdagen" (We mop the floor on Saturdays). To wipe up one spill, use "at tørre op" (to wipe up): "Jeg tørrer mælken op" (I wipe up the milk).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske gulv**, fordi det er meget beskidt.
sentence.en: I have to mop the floor because it is very dirty.

at vaske op.explanation: "At vaske op" means "to do the dishes". To ask whose turn it is, say: "Hvem vasker op i dag?" (Who is doing the dishes today?) Do not mix it up with "at vaske" (to wash). To say you wash a car, say: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske op** efter maden.
sentence.en: I have to do the dishes after the meal.

at vaske sig.explanation: "At vaske sig" means "to wash (oneself)". When you talk about another person, "sig" stays the same: "Han vasker sig" (He washes himself). To wash something else, use "at vaske" (to wash) and name the thing: "Jeg vasker bilen" (I wash the car).

sentence.da: Han skal **vaske sig** før maden.
sentence.en: He has to wash up before the meal.

at vaske tøj.explanation: "At vaske tøj" means "to do laundry". Literally, it is "to wash clothes". To say you do the dishes, use "at vaske op" (to do the dishes): "Jeg vasker op" (I do the dishes).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vaske tøj**, fordi jeg ikke har flere rene sokker.
sentence.en: I have to do laundry because I have no more clean socks.

at vedkende sig.explanation: "At vedkende sig" means "to acknowledge". The word "sig" always goes with it. To name what you acknowledge, put it after "sig": "Han vedkender sig sin fejl" (He acknowledges his mistake).

sentence.da: Han har svært ved at **vedkende sig** sine fejl.
sentence.en: He finds it hard to acknowledge his mistakes.

at vedligeholde.explanation: "At vedligeholde" means "to maintain". To say you keep a house in good shape, say: "Vi vedligeholder huset" (We maintain the house). To say someone claims something, use "at hævde" (to claim): "Hun hævder, at det er sandt" (She claims that it is true).

sentence.da: Man skal **vedligeholde** træværket hvert år, fordi regn skader det.
sentence.en: You must maintain the woodwork every year because rain damages it.

at vedlægge.explanation: "At vedlægge" means "to enclose". It is built from "ved" (by) and "at lægge" (to put). To say you put a document in with an email, name it after the verb: "Jeg vedlægger kvitteringen" (I enclose the receipt).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **vedlægge** mit CV til ansøgningen.
sentence.en: I would like to enclose my résumé with the application.

at vedrøre.explanation: "At vedrøre" means "to concern". To say a matter affects someone, put the person after the verb: "Sagen vedrører dig" (The matter concerns you). To start the subject of an email, use "Vedrørende" (Regarding), a form of this word: "Vedrørende din ansøgning" (Regarding your application).

sentence.da: Reglen kan **vedrøre** alle elever i skolen.
sentence.en: The rule can concern all students in the school.

at vedtage.explanation: "At vedtage" means "to pass (a law) or adopt". "Folketinget" is the Danish parliament. To say it made a law official, say: "Folketinget vedtog loven" (Parliament passed the law).

sentence.da: Byrådet vil **vedtage** det nye budget i næste uge.
sentence.en: The city council will pass the new budget next week.

at veje.explanation: "At veje" means "to weigh". To say how heavy you are, use the verb with a number: "Jeg vejer 70 kilo" (I weigh 70 kilos). To weigh an object on a scale, name the object after the verb: "Jeg vejer pakken" (I weigh the package).

sentence.da: Man kan **veje** maden på en vægt.
sentence.en: You can weigh the food on a scale.

at vejlede.explanation: "At vejlede" means "to guide or advise". It is built from "vej" (way) and "at lede" (to lead). To say someone helped you choose, say: "Hun vejledte mig i valget" (She advised me on the choice).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **vejlede** eleverne, når de skriver opgaven.
sentence.en: The teacher will guide the students when they write the assignment.

at veksle.explanation: "At veksle" means "to exchange (money)". To ask someone to break a big bill into smaller ones, say: "Kan du veksle en hundredkroneseddel?" (Can you break a hundred-krone bill?)

sentence.da: Hvor kan jeg **veksle** euro til danske kroner?
sentence.en: Where can I exchange euros for Danish kroner?

at velsigne.explanation: "At velsigne" means "to bless". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at signe" (to bless). To wish someone God's blessing, say: "Gud velsigne dig" (God bless you).

sentence.da: Præsten vil **velsigne** parret ved brylluppet.
sentence.en: The priest will bless the couple at the wedding.

at vende.explanation: "At vende" means "to turn". To turn something over, name it after the verb: "Jeg vender kortet" (I turn the card over). To turn in a direction, use "at dreje" (to turn): "Drej til venstre" (Turn left).

sentence.da: Du kan **vende** siden og læse videre.
sentence.en: You can turn the page and read on.

at vende sig.explanation: "At vende sig" means "to turn around". To say someone turns their own body, say: "Han vendte sig og smilede" (He turned around and smiled). Do not mix it up with "at vænne sig til" (to get used to). To say you are getting used to something, say: "Jeg vænner mig til kulden" (I am getting used to the cold).

sentence.da: Han vil **vende sig** og se på mig.
sentence.en: He wants to turn around and look at me.

at vende tilbage.explanation: "At vende tilbage" means "to return". To say you come back to a topic in a talk, add "til" (to): "Lad os vende tilbage til spørgsmålet" (Let us return to the question). To say you will answer someone later, say: "Jeg vender tilbage til dig" (I will get back to you).

sentence.da: Vi vil **vende tilbage** til Danmark næste år.
sentence.en: We want to return to Denmark next year.

at vente.explanation: "At vente" means "to wait". To say what you wait for, add "på" (for): "Jeg venter på bussen" (I am waiting for the bus). To say a woman is pregnant, use it for "to expect": "Hun venter barn" (She is expecting a baby).

sentence.da: Børn kan ikke **vente** til jul.
sentence.en: Kids cannot wait for Christmas.

at vente på.explanation: "At vente på" means "to wait for". To ask who someone is waiting for, keep "på" (for) at the end of the question: "Hvem venter du på?" (Who are you waiting for?)

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vente på** bussen.
sentence.en: I have to wait for the bus.

at verificere.explanation: "At verificere" means "to verify". To say you prove who you are, say: "at verificere sin identitet" (to verify your identity).

sentence.da: Journalisten vil **verificere** kilderne, fordi nyheden kan være falsk.
sentence.en: The journalist wants to verify the sources because the news may be false.

at vide.explanation: "At vide" means "to know (a fact)". To say you do not know something, say: "Jeg ved det ikke" (I do not know). To say you know a person, use "at kende" (to know someone): "Jeg kender Anna" (I know Anna).

sentence.da: Du skal **vide** dit telefonnummer.
sentence.en: You need to know your phone number.

at videreføre.explanation: "At videreføre" means "to continue". It is built from "videre" (onward) and "at føre" (to carry). To say you carry on something others began, name it after the verb: "De viderefører traditionen" (They carry on the tradition). To say you keep on doing something, use "at fortsætte" (to continue): "Jeg fortsætter med at læse" (I keep on reading).

sentence.da: Hun vil **videreføre** familiens firma, når hendes far går på pension.
sentence.en: She wants to carry on the family business when her father retires.

at videregive.explanation: "At videregive" means "to pass on". It is built from "videre" (onward) and "at give" (to give). To say you pass a message on, say: "Jeg videregiver beskeden til chefen" (I pass the message on to the boss).

sentence.da: Lægen må ikke **videregive** dine oplysninger til andre.
sentence.en: The doctor may not pass on your information to others.

at vidne.explanation: "At vidne" means "to testify". To name the person who testifies, use "et vidne" (a witness): "Hun er et vidne" (She is a witness). To say something shows a quality, add "om" (about): "Resultatet vidner om hårdt arbejde" (The result shows hard work).

sentence.da: Hun skal **vidne** i retten, fordi hun så ulykken.
sentence.en: She must testify in court because she saw the accident.

at vifte.explanation: "At vifte" means "to wave". To wave something back and forth, add "med" (with): "Han vifter med en avis" (He waves a newspaper). To wave to a person, use "at vinke" (to wave to someone): "Han vinkede til mig" (He waved to me). To name a fan, use the noun "en vifte" (a fan): "Jeg tænder for viften" (I turn on the fan).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **vifte** med små flag, når kongen kommer.
sentence.en: The children will wave small flags when the king comes.

at ville.explanation: "At ville" means "to want to or will". To say you want something, say: "Jeg vil have en kop kaffe" (I want a cup of coffee). To make it polite, add "gerne" (gladly): "Jeg vil gerne have en kop kaffe" (I would like a cup of coffee). To say you have to do something, use "skal" (have to): "Jeg skal gå" (I have to go).

sentence.da: Børn kan altid **ville** have mere.
sentence.en: Kids can always want more.

at vinde.explanation: "At vinde" means "to win". To say someone won a contest, name it after the verb: "Hun vandt konkurrencen" (She won the competition). The person who wins is "en vinder" (a winner).

sentence.da: Holdet med flest mål vil **vinde** kampen.
sentence.en: The team with the most goals will win the match.

at vinke.explanation: "At vinke" means "to wave". To say who you wave at, add "til" (to): "Han vinkede til mig" (He waved to me). To say you wave goodbye, add "farvel" (goodbye): "Han vinkede farvel" (He waved goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vinke** til dig, når toget kører.
sentence.en: I will wave to you when the train leaves.

at vippe.explanation: "At vippe" means "to tip or rock". To tell a child to stop rocking a chair, say: "Vip ikke med stolen!" (Do not rock the chair!) To name the playground seesaw, use the noun "en vippe" (a seesaw): "Børnene leger på vippen" (The children play on the seesaw).

sentence.da: Hvis bordet står skævt, kan det **vippe**.
sentence.en: If the table stands crooked, it can rock.

at virke.explanation: "At virke" means "to work or seem". To say a machine functions, use it for "to work": "Bilen virker ikke" (The car does not work). To say someone gives a certain impression, use it for "to seem": "Han virker træt" (He seems tired).

sentence.da: Telefonen vil ikke **virke** i dag.
sentence.en: The phone won't work today.

at vise.explanation: "At vise" means "to show". To show a thing, name it after the verb: "Jeg viser billedet" (I show the picture). To show something to a person, put the person right after the verb, with no "til" (to): "Hun viser mig bogen" (She shows me the book).

sentence.da: Kan du **vise** mig vej?
sentence.en: Can you show me the way?

at vise sig.explanation: "At vise sig" means "to turn out". To say what a person turned out to be, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Hun viste sig at være meget flink" (She turned out to be very nice).

sentence.da: Det kan **vise sig**, at han har ret.
sentence.en: It may turn out that he is right.

at visne.explanation: "At visne" means "to wither". To say a plant is slowly dying, add "hen" (away): "Planten visner hen" (The plant is withering away).

sentence.da: Blomsterne vil **visne**, når du glemmer at vande dem.
sentence.en: The flowers will wither when you forget to water them.

at visualisere.explanation: "At visualisere" means "to visualize". To say you picture something in your mind, say: "Jeg kan visualisere huset" (I can visualize the house). To say you show data as a graph, say: "at visualisere data" (to visualize data).

sentence.da: Vi bruger et diagram til at **visualisere** tallene.
sentence.en: We use a chart to visualize the figures.

at vokse.explanation: "At vokse" means "to grow". To say someone or something gets bigger, say: "Børn vokser hurtigt" (Children grow fast). To say where you spent your childhood, use "at vokse op" (to grow up): "Jeg voksede op i Odense" (I grew up in Odense). To grow tomatoes, use "at dyrke" (to cultivate): "Jeg dyrker tomater" (I grow tomatoes).

sentence.da: Planterne kan **vokse** meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: The plants can grow very fast.

at vokse op.explanation: "At vokse op" means "to grow up". It is built from "at vokse" (to grow) and "op" (up). To say where you spent your childhood, say: "Jeg voksede op i Odense" (I grew up in Odense). Without "op", "at vokse" means "to grow", as in "Træet vokser hurtigt" (The tree grows quickly).

sentence.da: Mine børn skal **vokse op** på landet.
sentence.en: My children will grow up in the countryside.

at vove.explanation: "At vove" means "to dare". To say you dare to do something, you can also use "at turde" (to dare): "Jeg tør ikke" (I do not dare).

sentence.da: Ingen vil **vove** at gå ind i det mørke hus.
sentence.en: No one will dare to go into the dark house.

at vride.explanation: "At vride" means "to twist or wring". To squeeze water out of a cloth, name the cloth: "Jeg vrider håndklædet" (I wring the towel). To say someone twists in pain, add "sig" (oneself): "Han vred sig af smerte" (He writhed in pain).

sentence.da: Du skal **vride** vandet ud af håndklædet.
sentence.en: You must wring the water out of the towel.

at vrimle.explanation: "At vrimle" means "to swarm or teem". To say what a place is full of, add "med" (with): "Gaden vrimler med mennesker" (The street teems with people).

sentence.da: Om sommeren kan stranden **vrimle** med børn og turister.
sentence.en: In the summer, the beach can swarm with children and tourists.

at vurdere.explanation: "At vurdere" means "to evaluate". To say an expert names a value for a house, say: "Huset bliver vurderet til tre millioner" (The house is valued at three million).

sentence.da: Lægen skal **vurdere**, om skaden er alvorlig.
sentence.en: The doctor must assess whether the injury is serious.

at vågne.explanation: "At vågne" means "to wake up". To say you woke up early, say: "Jeg vågnede tidligt" (I woke up early). When someone else wakes you, use "at vække" (to wake someone): "Min mor vækker mig" (My mother wakes me).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **vågne** klokken syv.
sentence.en: I have to wake up at seven.

at vågne op.explanation: "At vågne op" means "to wake up". It is built from "at vågne" (to wake up) and "op" (up). To say you woke in the night, say: "Jeg vågnede op midt om natten" (I woke up in the middle of the night).

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **vågne op** klokken seks.
sentence.en: I usually wake up at six.

at vædde.explanation: "At vædde" means "to bet". To name the event you bet on, use "på" (on): "Vi vædder på vejret" (We bet on the weather).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **vædde** på, at holdet vinder i aften.
sentence.en: I will bet that the team wins tonight.

at vække.explanation: "At vække" means "to wake (someone)". To say you wake another person, name the person: "Jeg vækker børnene" (I wake the children). To say you wake up yourself, use "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede tidligt" (I woke up early).

sentence.da: Kan du **vække** mig klokken seks?
sentence.en: Can you wake me at six?

at vælge.explanation: "At vælge" means "to choose". The noun "et valg" has two meanings. To say a decision is yours, use it for "a choice": "Det er dit valg" (It is your choice). To say people vote, use it for "an election": "Der er valg i dag" (There is an election today).

sentence.da: Du må **vælge** rød eller blå.
sentence.en: You may choose red or blue.

at vælte.explanation: "At vælte" means "to knock over or tip over". To say you knock something over, name it: "Jeg vælter koppen" (I knock over the cup). To say something goes over by itself, leave out the thing you knocked: "Træet væltede" (The tree fell over).

forms.en: I have knocked over / tipped over

sentence.da: Pas på, du kan **vælte** glasset!
sentence.en: Be careful, you might knock over the glass!

at vænne sig af med.explanation: "At vænne sig af med" means "to get out of the habit of". To say what you stopped doing, add "at" (to) and the verb: "Han vænnede sig af med at ryge" (He got out of the habit of smoking). To say you get used to something, use "at vænne sig til" (to get used to): "Jeg vænner mig til kulden" (I am getting used to the cold).

forms.en: to get out of the habit of
I get out of the habit of
I got out of the habit of

forms.da: jeg har vænnet mig af med
forms.en: I have gotten out of the habit of

sentence.da: Han vil **vænne sig af med** at spise sukker hver dag.
sentence.en: He wants to get out of the habit of eating sugar every day.

at vænne sig til.explanation: "At vænne sig til" means "to get used to". To say you are already used to something, use "vant til" (used to): "Jeg er vant til kulden" (I am used to the cold).

sentence.da: Det tager tid at **vænne sig til** et nyt sted.
sentence.en: It takes time to get used to a new place.

at værdsætte.explanation: "At værdsætte" means "to appreciate". It is built from "værd" (worth) and "at sætte" (to set). To say you are glad of someone's help, say: "Jeg værdsætter din hjælp" (I appreciate your help). To say something rises in value, use "at stige i værdi" (to rise in value): "Huset stiger i værdi" (The house is rising in value).

sentence.da: Man skal kunne **værdsætte** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: You have to be able to appreciate the small things in life.

at være.explanation: "At være" means "to be". To say how someone feels, use the form "er" (am, is, are): "Jeg er glad" (I am happy). The form "er" is the same for every person. For example, "han er" (he is), "vi er" (we are).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **være** hjemme i dag.
sentence.en: I want to be at home today.

at være bange for.explanation: "At være bange for" means "to be afraid of". To say what action you fear, add "at" (to) before the verb: "Jeg er bange for at falde" (I am afraid of falling).

sentence.da: Børn kan **være bange for** mørket.
sentence.en: Children can be afraid of the dark.

at være enig.explanation: "At være enig" means "to agree". Literally, it is "to be in agreement". To say who you agree with, add "med" (with): "Jeg er enig med dig" (I agree with you). To say what you agree with, add "i" (in): "Jeg er enig i planen" (I agree with the plan).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **være enig** i det.
sentence.en: I can agree with that.

at være i tvivl.explanation: "At være i tvivl" means "to be in doubt". To name the subject of your doubt, add "om" (about): "Jeg er i tvivl om svaret" (I am in doubt about the answer).

sentence.da: Når man ikke ved svaret, kan man **være i tvivl**.
sentence.en: When you do not know the answer, you can be in doubt.

at være kærester.explanation: "At være kærester" means "to be dating". One person in the couple is "en kæreste" (a boyfriend or girlfriend). For example, "Hun er min kæreste" (She is my girlfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **være kærester** med dig.
sentence.en: I would like us to be a couple.

at være med.explanation: "At være med" means "to take part or be in on it". To invite someone to join, ask: "Er du med?" (Are you in?) To say you do not follow what is being said, say: "Jeg er ikke helt med" (I am not quite following).

forms.en: to take part / be in on it

sentence.da: Vil du **være med**, når vi spiller fodbold?
sentence.en: Do you want to join in when we play soccer?

at være nødt til.explanation: "At være nødt til" means "to have to". To say you have no other choice, say: "Jeg er nødt til at gå nu" (I have to go now). To say what you are going to do, use "skal" (am going to): "Jeg skal på arbejde" (I am going to work).

sentence.da: Hvis bussen er væk, kan vi **være nødt til** at gå.
sentence.en: If the bus is gone, we may have to walk.

at være oppe at køre.explanation: "At være oppe at køre" means "to be worked up". To say someone is tense before an event, say: "Hun var helt oppe at køre før brylluppet" (She was all worked up before the wedding).

forms.da: Han var oppe at køre i går
Vær ikke så oppe at køre
forms.en: Do not be so worked up

sentence.da: Han plejer at **være oppe at køre**, når der er eksamen.
sentence.en: He tends to be worked up when there is an exam.

at være på bar bund.explanation: "At være på bar bund" means "to be at a total loss". Literally, it is "to be on bare bottom". The word "bar" (bare) also appears in "bare fødder" (bare feet).

forms.en: I am at a total loss
She was at a total loss
We are at a total loss

sentence.da: Han vil **være på bar bund** til eksamen, fordi han ikke har læst.
sentence.en: He will be at a total loss at the exam because he has not studied.

at være på herrens mark.explanation: "At være på Herrens mark" means "to be completely lost". Literally, it is "to be on the Lord's field". To tell someone they are wrong, say: "Der er du helt på Herrens mark" (You are completely off there).

forms.da: Jeg er helt på Herrens mark
Vi var helt på Herrens mark

related.da: at være helt ude at svømme
related.en: to be out of your depth
to be on the right track

sentence.da: Han kan **være på Herrens mark**, når han ikke har læst opgaven.
sentence.en: He can be completely lost when he has not read the assignment.

at være på vej.explanation: "At være på vej" means "to be on one's way". To say where you are heading, add the place: "Jeg er på vej hjem" (I am on my way home). To name a city you are heading to, add "til" (to): "Han er på vej til Aarhus" (He is on his way to Aarhus).

forms.en: I have been on my way

sentence.da: Vi skal **være på vej** inden otte.
sentence.en: We must be on our way before eight.

at være syg.explanation: "At være syg" means "to be sick". To say you are getting sick, use "at blive syg" (to become sick): "Jeg bliver syg" (I am getting sick).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **være syg** i ferien.
sentence.en: I do not want to be sick on vacation.

at være træt af.explanation: "At være træt af" means "to be tired of". To say something annoys you, put it after "af": "Jeg er træt af regnen" (I am tired of the rain). To say you are sleepy, leave out "af": "Jeg er træt" (I am tired).

sentence.da: Man kan let **være træt af** at vente.
sentence.en: You can easily get tired of waiting.

at være ude i god tid.explanation: "At være ude i god tid" means "to be well ahead of time". To say you left plenty of time before a flight, say: "Vi er ude i god tid til flyet" (We are in good time for the plane). To say you have plenty of time, use "god tid" (plenty of time) with "have" (have): "Vi har god tid" (We have plenty of time).

forms.da: Vi er ude i god tid
forms.en: We are well ahead of time

forms.da: Er du ude i god tid?
forms.en: Are you well ahead of time?

forms.da: Man skal være ude i god tid

sentence.da: Vi skal **være ude i god tid**, fordi flyet letter klokken seks.
sentence.en: We must be well ahead of time because the plane takes off at six.

at være uenig.explanation: "At være uenig" means "to disagree". To say you disagree with a person, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uenig med dig" (I disagree with you). To name what you disagree about, add "i" (in): "Vi er uenige i det" (We disagree about that).

sentence.da: Det er okay at **være uenig** med en ven.
sentence.en: It is okay to disagree with a friend.

at være vant til.explanation: "At være vant til" means "to be used to". To say you are used to a thing, put it after "til" (to): "Hun er vant til støjen" (She is used to the noise). To say you are used to doing an action, add "at" (to) and the verb: "Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op" (I am used to getting up early).

related.en: to be in the habit of

sentence.da: Efter et år vil du **være vant til** kulden.
sentence.en: After a year, you will be used to the cold.

at være ved at.explanation: "At være ved at" means "to be about to or be in the middle of". To say something is about to happen, say: "Toget er ved at køre" (The train is about to leave). To say you are busy doing something right now, say: "Jeg er ved at spise" (I am in the middle of eating).

forms.en: to be about to / be in the middle of
I am about to / am in the middle of
I was about to / was in the middle of
I have been about to / been in the middle of

sentence.da: Børnene kan **være ved at** falde i søvn.
sentence.en: The children may be about to fall asleep.

at være vild med.explanation: "At være vild med" means "to be crazy about". Literally, it is "to be wild with". To say you love a food, put it after "med": "Jeg er vild med pizza" (I love pizza). To say you are crazy about a person, do the same: "Hun er vild med ham" (She is crazy about him).

sentence.da: Du vil **være vild med** den her film.
sentence.en: You will love this movie.

at være væk.explanation: "At være væk" means "to be gone". To say a person has left, say: "Han er væk" (He is gone). To say a thing has disappeared, say: "Min telefon er væk" (My phone is gone).

sentence.da: Han skal **være væk** i to dage.
sentence.en: He has to be away for two days.

at værne om.explanation: "At værne om" means "to protect or safeguard". The small word "om" (about) must always follow "værne". To say what you protect, put it after "om": "Vi skal værne om friheden" (We must protect freedom).

sentence.da: Vi bør **værne om** vores natur og vores sprog.
sentence.en: We should protect our nature and our language.

en vaccination.explanation: "En vaccination" means "a vaccination". To say you are going to get the shot, say: "Jeg skal have en vaccination" (I am going to get a vaccination). To talk about the medicine in the shot, use "en vaccine" (a vaccine): "Vaccinen virker" (The vaccine works).

sentence.da: Børnene får en **vaccination** hos lægen.
sentence.en: The children get a vaccination at the doctor's.

en vaccine.explanation: "En vaccine" means "a vaccine". To say what the vaccine is against, add "mod" (against): "en vaccine mod mæslinger" (a vaccine against measles). To talk about the shot you get at the doctor, use "en vaccination" (a vaccination): "Jeg skal have en vaccination" (I am going to get a vaccination).

sentence.da: Lægen gav mig en **vaccine** mod influenza.
sentence.en: The doctor gave me a vaccine against the flu.

en vaffel.explanation: "En vaffel" means "a waffle". It has a second meaning, the crisp cone for ice cream. For example, "Jeg vil gerne have en is i vaffel" (I would like an ice cream in a cone).

sentence.da: Til dessert får jeg en **vaffel** med is.
sentence.en: For dessert I get a waffle with ice cream.

en vagt.explanation: "En vagt" means "a guard or shift". When you mean a person who watches a place, it means "a guard": "Vagten står ved porten" (The guard stands at the gate). When you mean a work period, it means "a shift": "Min vagt slutter klokken seks" (My shift ends at six). To say you are on duty, use "at have vagt" (to be on duty) without "en": "Hun har vagt i dag" (She is on duty today).

sentence.da: Han har **vagt** på hospitalet i nat.
sentence.en: He is on duty at the hospital tonight.

en vagtlæge.explanation: "En vagtlæge" means "an on-call doctor". It is built from "vagt" (duty) and "læge" (doctor). In Denmark, when your own doctor's office is closed in the evening, at night or at the weekend, you call "lægevagten" (the out-of-hours doctor service) to reach one.

sentence.da: Om natten kan du få hjælp fra en **vagtlæge**.
sentence.en: At night you can get help from an on-call doctor.

en valgkamp.explanation: "En valgkamp" means "an election campaign". It is built from "valg" (election) and "kamp" (fight), so it is literally a fight for votes. To say the campaign has started, use "i gang" (under way): "Nu er valgkampen i gang" (The election campaign has started).

sentence.da: I en **valgkamp** prøver partierne at vinde vælgernes stemmer.
sentence.en: In an election campaign the parties try to win the voters' votes.

en valgkreds.explanation: "En valgkreds" means "a constituency". It is built from "valg" (election) and "kreds" (district). To ask which constituency someone lives in, say: "Hvilken valgkreds bor du i?" (Which constituency do you live in?)

sentence.da: Man stemmer i den **valgkreds**, hvor man bor.
sentence.en: You vote in the constituency where you live.

en valgmulighed.explanation: "En valgmulighed" means "an option". It is built from "valg" (choice) and "mulighed" (possibility). To say there are several options, use the plural: "Der er flere valgmuligheder" (There are several options).

related.en: something you choose to leave out

sentence.da: Der er kun én **valgmulighed**, og det er at vente.
sentence.en: There is only one option, and that is to wait.

en valnød.explanation: "En valnød" means "a walnut". The last part, "nød" (nut), is also in "en jordnød" (a peanut).

sentence.da: Jeg knækker en **valnød** og spiser den.
sentence.en: I crack a walnut and eat it.

en valuta.explanation: "En valuta" means "a currency". To talk about money from another country, add "udenlandsk" (foreign): "udenlandsk valuta" (foreign currency).

sentence.da: Euro er den **valuta**, de bruger i Tyskland.
sentence.en: The euro is the currency they use in Germany.

en vampyr.explanation: "En vampyr" means "a vampire". Danish spells it with a "y" in the last part, where English has an "i".

sentence.da: En **vampyr** drikker blod og sover om dagen.
sentence.en: A vampire drinks blood and sleeps during the day.

en vandflaske.explanation: "En vandflaske" means "a water bottle". It is built from "vand" (water) and "flaske" (bottle).

sentence.da: Jeg fylder min **vandflaske** med koldt vand.
sentence.en: I fill my water bottle with cold water.

en vandhane.explanation: "En vandhane" means "a faucet or tap". It is built from "vand" (water) and "hane", which means "rooster" and also "tap". To tell someone to turn off the tap, say: "Luk for vandhanen" (Turn off the faucet).

sentence.da: Der drypper vand fra en **vandhane** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: Water is dripping from a faucet in the kitchen.

en vandkande.explanation: "En vandkande" means "a watering can". It is built from "vand" (water) and "kande" (jug), the same "kande" as in "en kaffekande" (a coffee pot).

sentence.da: Jeg vander blomsterne med en **vandkande**.
sentence.en: I water the flowers with a watering can.

en vandkaraffel.explanation: "En vandkaraffel" means "a water carafe". It is built from "vand" (water) and "karaffel" (carafe).

sentence.da: Der står en **vandkaraffel** på bordet.
sentence.en: There is a water carafe on the table.

en vandmand.explanation: "En vandmand" means "a jellyfish". It is built from "vand" (water) and "mand" (man). The plural is "vandmænd", with "æ" instead of "a".

sentence.da: Hvis du rører en **vandmand**, kan den brænde dig.
sentence.en: If you touch a jellyfish, it can burn you.

en vandmelon.explanation: "En vandmelon" means "a watermelon". It is built from "vand" (water) and "melon" (melon). To ask for a piece, say: "en skive vandmelon" (a slice of watermelon).

sentence.da: På en varm dag spiser vi **vandmelon**.
sentence.en: On a warm day, we eat watermelon.

en vandpyt.explanation: "En vandpyt" means "a puddle". It is built from "vand" (water) and "pyt" (puddle). The word "pyt" is also what Danes say to let something go: "Pyt!" (Never mind!)

sentence.da: Jeg trådte i en stor **vandpyt** og blev våd.
sentence.en: I stepped in a big puddle and got wet.

en vandregning.explanation: "En vandregning" means "a water bill". It is built from "vand" (water) and "regning" (bill). In a restaurant, "regning" also means the check. For example, "Regningen, tak" (The check, please).

sentence.da: Vi sparer på vandet og får en lav **vandregning**.
sentence.en: We save on water and get a low water bill.

en vandretur.explanation: "En vandretur" means "a hike". It is built from "at vandre" (to hike) and "tur" (trip), the same "tur" as in "en cykeltur" (a bike ride).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en lang **vandretur** i weekenden.
sentence.en: We are going on a long hike this weekend.

en vane.explanation: "En vane" means "a habit". To say you have a habit of doing something, use "at have for vane" (to be in the habit of) with "at" and a verb: "Jeg har for vane at gå en tur" (I am in the habit of going for a walk).

sentence.da: Det er en dårlig **vane** at komme for sent.
sentence.en: It is a bad habit to be late.

en vaniljekrans.explanation: "En vaniljekrans" means "a vanilla butter cookie". It is a traditional Danish Christmas cookie. It is built from "vanilje" (vanilla) and "krans" (wreath).

sentence.da: En **vaniljekrans** er en lille, sprød ring af smør, mel og sukker.
sentence.en: A vanilla butter cookie is a small, crisp ring of butter, flour and sugar.

en vanskelighed.explanation: "En vanskelighed" means "a difficulty". It comes from the adjective "vanskelig" (difficult). To say someone has difficulty doing something, use the plural with "med" (with): "Hun har vanskeligheder med at høre" (She has difficulty hearing).

sentence.da: Den største **vanskelighed** er, at vi mangler tid.
sentence.en: The biggest difficulty is that we are short of time.

en vante.explanation: "En vante" means "a mitten". A glove with a space for each finger is "en handske" (a glove). For example, "Jeg har røde handsker på" (I am wearing red gloves).

sentence.da: Jeg har mistet min ene **vante**, så min hånd fryser.
sentence.en: I have lost one of my mittens, so my hand is freezing.

en vare.explanation: "En vare" means "an item or product". To talk about goods in a shop, use the plural "varer" (goods): "Butikken har mange varer" (The shop has many goods). For a thing you own, use "en ting" (a thing): "Jeg har mange ting i skabet" (I have many things in the closet).

sentence.da: Denne **vare** koster kun tyve kroner.
sentence.en: This item costs only twenty kroner.

en varedeklaration.explanation: "En varedeklaration" means "a product label". It is built from "vare" (product) and "deklaration" (declaration). To tell someone to check what is in the food, say: "Læs varedeklarationen" (Read the product label).

sentence.da: På en **varedeklaration** står der, hvad varen indeholder.
sentence.en: A product label says what the product contains.

en vareprøve.explanation: "En vareprøve" means "a product sample". To say the sample costs nothing, add "gratis" (free): "en gratis vareprøve" (a free product sample).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **vareprøve** af den nye creme.
sentence.en: I got a product sample of the new cream.

en varevogn.explanation: "En varevogn" means "a van". It is built from "varer" (goods) and "vogn" (wagon), the same "vogn" as in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart).

sentence.da: Vi flytter vores møbler i en **varevogn**.
sentence.en: We are moving our furniture in a van.

en variation.explanation: "En variation" means "a variation". To say what the variation is based on, add "over" (on): "en variation over en gammel opskrift" (a variation on an old recipe).

sentence.da: Det er sundt med **variation** i det, man spiser.
sentence.en: It is healthy to have variation in what you eat.

en varmebølge.explanation: "En varmebølge" means "a heat wave". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "bølge" (wave). To say a heat wave is on its way, say: "Der kommer en varmebølge" (A heat wave is coming).

sentence.da: Under en **varmebølge** bør man drikke meget vand.
sentence.en: During a heat wave you should drink a lot of water.

en varmepumpe.explanation: "En varmepumpe" means "a heat pump". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "pumpe" (pump).

sentence.da: Vi varmer huset op med en **varmepumpe**.
sentence.en: We heat the house with a heat pump.

en varmerekord.explanation: "En varmerekord" means "a record high temperature". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "rekord" (record). To talk about the opposite, use "en kulderekord" (a record low): "Der blev sat en kulderekord i går" (A record low was set yesterday).

sentence.da: I dag blev der sat en ny **varmerekord** i Danmark.
sentence.en: Today a new record high was set in Denmark.

en vase.explanation: "En vase" means "a vase". To say what is in it, add "med" (with): "en vase med roser" (a vase with roses).

sentence.da: Hun sætter blomsterne i en **vase** med vand.
sentence.en: She puts the flowers in a vase with water.

en vask.explanation: "En vask" means "a sink". It comes from the verb "at vaske" (to wash). To say you wash your hands, use the verb: "Jeg vasker mine hænder" (I wash my hands).

sentence.da: Vi har en stor **vask** i køkkenet.
sentence.en: We have a big sink in the kitchen.

en vaskekælder.explanation: "En vaskekælder" means "a laundry room". It is built from "vaske" (to wash) and "kælder" (basement). In Denmark, an apartment building can have one that all the residents share.

sentence.da: Vores tøj vaskes i en **vaskekælder** under huset.
sentence.en: Our clothes are washed in a laundry room under the house.

en vaskemaskine.explanation: "En vaskemaskine" means "a washing machine". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you start it, use "sætte i gang" (to get going): "Jeg sætter vaskemaskinen i gang" (I start the washing machine).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker tøj i en **vaskemaskine**.
sentence.en: I wash clothes in a washing machine.

en vatpind.explanation: "En vatpind" means "a cotton swab". It is built from "vat" (cotton wool) and "pind" (stick), the same "pind" as in "en spisepind" (a chopstick).

sentence.da: Hun tager makeup af med en **vatpind**.
sentence.en: She takes off makeup with a cotton swab.

en vedhæftet fil.explanation: "En vedhæftet fil" means "an attachment". Literally, it is "an attached file". To tell someone to look at the attachment in an email, write: "Se den vedhæftede fil" (See the attached file).

sentence.da: Jeg sender dig en **vedhæftet fil** med billederne fra turen.
sentence.en: I am sending you an attachment with the pictures from the trip.

en veganer.explanation: "En veganer" means "a vegan". Do not mix it up with "en vegetar" (a vegetarian). For example, "Han er vegetar og spiser æg" (He is a vegetarian and eats eggs).

sentence.da: Hun er **veganer** og spiser hverken kød eller ost.
sentence.en: She is a vegan and eats neither meat nor cheese.

en vegetar.explanation: "En vegetar" means "a vegetarian". To describe food, use "vegetarisk" (vegetarian): "en vegetarisk ret" (a vegetarian dish).

sentence.da: En **vegetar** spiser ikke kød.
sentence.en: A vegetarian does not eat meat.

en vej.explanation: "En vej" means "a road". It has a second meaning, "a way" or route. For example, "Hvilken vej skal jeg gå?" (Which way should I go?). To ask for directions, say "at spørge om vej" (to ask for directions), with no "en" before "vej": "Jeg vil spørge om vej" (I will ask for directions).

sentence.da: Bilen kører på en lang **vej**.
sentence.en: The car drives on a long road.

en vejleder.explanation: "En vejleder" means "a supervisor". It comes from the verb "at vejlede" (to guide).

sentence.da: Min **vejleder** læser mit speciale og siger, hvad jeg kan forbedre.
sentence.en: My supervisor reads my thesis and says what I can improve.

en vejledning.explanation: "En vejledning" means "a guide". It is the noun for the verb "at vejlede" (to guide). To say what the guide is for, add "til" (for): "en vejledning til programmet" (a guide for the program).

sentence.da: Du kan finde en **vejledning** på hjemmesiden.
sentence.en: You can find a guide on the website.

en vejrmelding.explanation: "En vejrmelding" means "a weather report". It is built from "vejr" (weather) and "melding" (message), the same "melding" as in "en fejlmelding" (an error message).

sentence.da: Jeg lytter til en **vejrmelding** om regn i morgen.
sentence.en: I listen to a weather report about rain tomorrow.

en vejrudsigt.explanation: "En vejrudsigt" means "a weather forecast". It is built from "vejr" (weather) and "udsigt" (outlook). "Udsigt" also means "a view" by itself. For example, "Der er en flot udsigt" (There is a great view).

sentence.da: Der er en **vejrudsigt** på tv hver aften.
sentence.en: There is a weather forecast on TV every evening.

en vejviser.explanation: "En vejviser" means "a signpost". It is built from "vej" (road) and "viser" (pointer, from "at vise", to show). It has a second meaning, a printed directory of addresses. For example, "Jeg slog adressen op i vejviseren" (I looked up the address in the directory).

sentence.da: Ved krydset viser en **vejviser**, hvilken vej vi skal gå.
sentence.en: At the crossing a signpost shows which way we must go.

en vekselkurs.explanation: "En vekselkurs" means "an exchange rate". It is built from "at veksle" (to exchange) and "kurs" (rate).

sentence.da: Hvad er den aktuelle **vekselkurs** mellem kroner og euro?
sentence.en: What is the current exchange rate between kroner and euros?

en velsignelse.explanation: "En velsignelse" means "a blessing". It also means something that is a great help. For example, "Din hjælp er en velsignelse" (Your help is a blessing).

sentence.da: Præsten gav parret sin **velsignelse** efter brylluppet.
sentence.en: The priest gave the couple his blessing after the wedding.

en ven.explanation: "En ven" means "a friend". It is the word for a friend of either sex. For example, "Hun er min bedste ven" (She is my best friend). Do not mix it up with "en kæreste" (boyfriend or girlfriend). For another example, "Han er min kæreste" (He is my boyfriend).

sentence.da: Jeg spiller fodbold med min **ven**.
sentence.en: I play soccer with my friend.

en veninde.explanation: "En veninde" means "a female friend". To say a male friend, use "en ven" (a friend): "Han er min ven" (He is my friend).

sentence.da: Hun er min **veninde**, ikke min kæreste.
sentence.en: She is my female friend, not my girlfriend.

en vennegruppe.explanation: "En vennegruppe" means "a group of friends". It is built from "venner" (friends) and "gruppe" (group), the same "gruppe" as in "en studiegruppe" (a study group).

sentence.da: Min **vennegruppe** mødes hver fredag.
sentence.en: My group of friends meets every Friday.

en venteliste.explanation: "En venteliste" means "a waiting list". To say you are on a waiting list, use "stå på venteliste" (to be on a waiting list) without "en": "Hun står på venteliste til en lejlighed" (She is on the waiting list for an apartment).

sentence.da: Vi står på **venteliste** til en plads i børnehaven.
sentence.en: We are on the waiting list for a spot in kindergarten.

en ventetid.explanation: "En ventetid" means "a wait time". It is built from "at vente" (to wait) and "en tid" (a time). To ask how long you will wait, say: "Hvor lang er ventetiden?" (How long is the wait?)

sentence.da: Der er lang **ventetid** hos lægen.
sentence.en: There is a long wait at the doctor's office.

en ventilator.explanation: "En ventilator" means "a fan", as in the machine that moves air. A fan of a team is "en fan" (a fan). For example, "Jeg er fan af holdet" (I am a fan of the team).

sentence.da: Det er varmt, og jeg tænder en **ventilator**.
sentence.en: It is hot, and I am turning on a fan.

en verden.explanation: "En verden" means "a world". To say something happens everywhere, use "i hele verden" (all over the world): "Man spiller fodbold i hele verden" (People play soccer all over the world). To say something is the best in the world, add "s" to "verden": "Det er verdens bedste kage" (It is the best cake in the world).

sentence.da: Jeg vil rejse rundt i **verden**.
sentence.en: I want to travel around the world.

en verdensdel.explanation: "En verdensdel" means "a continent". It is built from "verden" (world) and "del" (part), so it is literally "world part".

sentence.da: Europa er den **verdensdel**, hvor Danmark ligger.
sentence.en: Europe is the continent where Denmark is located.

en verdenskrig.explanation: "En verdenskrig" means "a world war". It is built from "verden" (world) and "krig" (war). To name the two world wars, say "første verdenskrig" (the First World War) and "anden verdenskrig" (the Second World War).

sentence.da: Min oldefar var soldat under den første **verdenskrig**.
sentence.en: My great-grandfather was a soldier during the First World War.

en version.explanation: "En version" means "a version". To talk about a new release, say: "den nye version af appen" (the new version of the app). To talk about one person's account of what happened, say: "Hun fortalte sin version" (She told her version).

sentence.da: Filmen findes i en dansk **version**.
sentence.en: The film exists in a Danish version.

en vest.explanation: "En vest" means "a vest", as in the sleeveless garment worn over a shirt. The word is also in "en redningsvest" (a life jacket). For example, "Børnene har redningsveste på" (The children are wearing life jackets).

sentence.da: Min onkel har en grå **vest** over skjorten.
sentence.en: My uncle has a gray vest over his shirt.

en veteran.explanation: "En veteran" means "a veteran". It also means a very experienced person. For example, "Hun er en veteran i branchen" (She is a veteran in the industry). As the first part of a compound, it means old but well kept. For another example, "en veteranbil" (a vintage car).

sentence.da: Han er **veteran** efter mange år i hæren.
sentence.en: He is a veteran after many years in the army.

en vicepræsident.explanation: "En vicepræsident" means "a vice president". It is built from "vice" (deputy) and "præsident" (president). Denmark has a monarch, not a president. To talk about the vice president of the USA, say: "USA's vicepræsident" (the vice president of the USA).

sentence.da: En **vicepræsident** kan overtage, hvis præsidenten bliver syg.
sentence.en: A vice president can take over if the president gets sick.

en vicevært.explanation: "En vicevært" means "a caretaker or janitor". It is built from "vice" (deputy) and "vært" (host), so it is literally a deputy host.

sentence.da: Når lyset i trappen er i stykker, ringer vi til en **vicevært**.
sentence.en: When the light on the stairs is broken, we call a caretaker.

en videnskab.explanation: "En videnskab" means "a science". To name the school subject science, use "naturfag" (natural science subjects): "Vi har naturfag i dag" (We have science today).

sentence.da: Biologi er en **videnskab**, der studerer alt levende.
sentence.en: Biology is a science that studies everything living.

en videnskabsmand.explanation: "En videnskabsmand" means "a scientist". It is built from "videnskab" (science) and "mand" (man), a pattern also used in "en brandmand" (a firefighter).

sentence.da: Den kendte **videnskabsmand** arbejder på et laboratorium.
sentence.en: The famous scientist works at a laboratory.

en video.explanation: "En video" means "a video". To say you record a video, use "at optage" (to record): "Jeg optager en video" (I record a video).

sentence.da: Jeg har set en sjov **video** på nettet.
sentence.en: I watched a funny video online.

en vielsesring.explanation: "En vielsesring" means "a wedding ring". It is built from "vielse" (wedding ceremony) and "ring" (ring). Do not mix it up with "en forlovelsesring" (an engagement ring). For example, "Hun fik en forlovelsesring i går" (She got an engagement ring yesterday).

sentence.da: Han har en **vielsesring** på fingeren.
sentence.en: He has a wedding ring on his finger.

en vikar.explanation: "En vikar" means "a substitute teacher". To say a temp in another job, add the place: "en vikar på kontoret" (a temp at the office).

sentence.da: Vi får en **vikar**, fordi vores lærer er syg.
sentence.en: We get a substitute because our teacher is sick.

en viking.explanation: "En viking" means "a Viking". To talk about a Viking ship, use "et vikingeskib" (a Viking ship): "Vi så et vikingeskib på museet" (We saw a Viking ship at the museum).

sentence.da: En **viking** sejlede over havet i et langt skib.
sentence.en: A Viking sailed over the sea in a long ship.

en vilje.explanation: "En vilje" means "a will", as in willpower. To say you did something on purpose, use "med vilje" (on purpose), without "en": "Han gjorde det med vilje" (He did it on purpose).

sentence.da: Det kræver **vilje** at holde op med at ryge.
sentence.en: It takes willpower to quit smoking.

en villa.explanation: "En villa" means "a detached house". Unlike the English word "villa", it does not have to be fancy: in Denmark it is an ordinary family house.

sentence.da: De bor i en stor **villa** med have.
sentence.en: They live in a big detached house with a garden.

en vin.explanation: "En vin" means "a wine". To name the color of the wine, join it to "vin": "en rødvin" (a red wine) or "en hvidvin" (a white wine). To order a drink, say: "et glas vin" (a glass of wine).

sentence.da: **Vin** er lavet af druer.
sentence.en: Wine is made from grapes.

en vinbar.explanation: "En vinbar" means "a wine bar". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "bar" (bar).

sentence.da: Vi drikker rødvin på en hyggelig **vinbar**.
sentence.en: We drink red wine at a cozy wine bar.

en vinder.explanation: "En vinder" means "a winner". It comes from the verb "at vinde" (to win). The opposite is "en taber" (a loser). For example, "Han er en dårlig taber" (He is a bad loser).

sentence.da: Hvem bliver **vinder** af kampen i aften?
sentence.en: Who will be the winner of the match tonight?

en vindmølle.explanation: "En vindmølle" means "a wind turbine or windmill". It is built from "vind" (wind) and "mølle" (mill).

sentence.da: Vi kan se en stor **vindmølle** fra vinduet.
sentence.en: We can see a big wind turbine from the window.

en vindrue.explanation: "En vindrue" means "a grape". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "drue" (grape). To talk about a bunch of grapes, say: "en klase vindruer" (a bunch of grapes).

sentence.da: Han spiser en grøn **vindrue** ad gangen.
sentence.en: He eats one green grape at a time.

en vindueskarm.explanation: "En vindueskarm" means "a windowsill". To say something sits on the windowsill, Danish uses "i" (in) where English uses "on": "Katten sidder i vindueskarmen" (The cat sits on the windowsill).

sentence.da: Der står en lille plante i hver **vindueskarm**.
sentence.en: There is a small plant on every windowsill.

en vinduesplads.explanation: "En vinduesplads" means "a window seat". The opposite is "en gangplads" (an aisle seat). For example, "Jeg vil gerne have en gangplads" (I would like an aisle seat).

sentence.da: Fra en **vinduesplads** kan man se skyerne.
sentence.en: From a window seat you can see the clouds.

en vinduespudsning.explanation: "En vinduespudsning" means "a window cleaning". It comes from "at pudse" (to polish). To say you shine your shoes, use the same verb: "Jeg pudser mine sko" (I polish my shoes).

sentence.da: Vi har bestilt en **vinduespudsning**, fordi vinduerne er meget snavsede.
sentence.en: We have ordered a window cleaning because the windows are very dirty.

en vinduesvisker.explanation: "En vinduesvisker" means "a windshield wiper". It is built from "vindue" (window) and "visker" (wiper).

sentence.da: Det regner meget, så jeg tænder for min **vinduesvisker**.
sentence.en: It is raining a lot, so I turn on my windshield wiper.

en vinge.explanation: "En vinge" means "a wing", as in the wing of a bird or a plane. For the wing of a building, use "en fløj" (a wing): "Slottet har to fløje" (The castle has two wings).

sentence.da: Fuglen kan ikke flyve, fordi den har brækket en **vinge**.
sentence.en: The bird cannot fly because it has broken a wing.

en vinhandel.explanation: "En vinhandel" means "a wine shop". The word "handel" (trade) is also in "en blomsterhandel" (a flower shop).

sentence.da: Du kan få hjælp til at vælge en god rødvin i en **vinhandel**.
sentence.en: You can get help choosing a good red wine in a wine shop.

en vinkel.explanation: "En vinkel" means "an angle". In math, it is the angle between two lines. For example, "en ret vinkel" (a right angle). To talk about a way of looking at something, say: "Jeg ser det fra en anden vinkel" (I see it from another angle).

sentence.da: Her er en **vinkel** på halvfems grader.
sentence.en: Here is an angle of ninety degrees.

en vinliste.explanation: "En vinliste" means "a wine list". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "liste" (list), the same "liste" as in "en gæsteliste" (a guest list). To ask the waiter for it, say: "Må jeg se vinlisten?" (May I see the wine list?)

sentence.da: På en **vinliste** står mange slags vin.
sentence.en: A wine list shows many kinds of wine.

en vinter.explanation: "En vinter" means "a winter". To say what happens every winter, use "om vinteren" (in the winter): "Om vinteren er det koldt" (In the winter it is cold).

sentence.da: En **vinter** i Danmark er kold og mørk.
sentence.en: A winter in Denmark is cold and dark.

en vinterbader.explanation: "En vinterbader" means "a winter swimmer". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "at bade" (to swim). "At bade" means going into the sea or a lake for fun. For example, "Vi bader i søen" (We swim in the lake).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **vinterbader** og svømmer i havet hver morgen.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a winter swimmer and swims in the sea every morning.

en vinterdag.explanation: "En vinterdag" means "a winter day". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "dag" (day), and the same "vinter" is in "en vinterferie" (a winter break).

sentence.da: På en **vinterdag** er det mørkt klokken fire.
sentence.en: On a winter day it is dark at four o'clock.

en vinterferie.explanation: "En vinterferie" means "a winter break". In Denmark, school children have it in February.

sentence.da: Børnene har **vinterferie** og er fri fra skole i en uge.
sentence.en: The children are on winter break and are off from school for a week.

en vinterjakke.explanation: "En vinterjakke" means "a winter jacket". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "jakke" (jacket), the same "jakke" as in "en læderjakke" (a leather jacket).

sentence.da: I sneen har jeg en **vinterjakke** på.
sentence.en: In the snow I wear a winter jacket.

en vinternat.explanation: "En vinternat" means "a winter night". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "nat" (night). To say you slept badly last night, use "i nat" (last night): "Jeg sov dårligt i nat" (I slept badly last night).

sentence.da: Det er koldt og mørkt på en **vinternat**.
sentence.en: It is cold and dark on a winter night.

en vinterstøvle.explanation: "En vinterstøvle" means "a winter boot". To talk about more than one boot, use the plural: "Jeg tager vinterstøvler på" (I put on winter boots).

sentence.da: Min venstre **vinterstøvle** er våd af sne.
sentence.en: My left winter boot is wet from snow.

en violin.explanation: "En violin" means "a violin". Danish has a second word, "en fiol" (a fiddle). For example, "Han spiller fiol til dans" (He plays fiddle for dancing).

sentence.da: Min datter øver sig på **violin** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter practices the violin every day.

en vippe.explanation: "En vippe" means "a seesaw". The same word is in "en øjenvippe" (an eyelash). For example, "Hun har lange øjenvipper" (She has long eyelashes).

sentence.da: To børn sidder på hver sin ende af en **vippe**.
sentence.en: Two children sit at each end of a seesaw.

en virkelighed.explanation: "En virkelighed" means "a reality". A very common phrase is "i virkeligheden" (in reality). For example, "I virkeligheden er han meget genert" (In reality, he is very shy).

sentence.da: Eventyret er en historie, ikke **virkelighed**.
sentence.en: The fairy tale is a story, not reality.

en virkning.explanation: "En virkning" means "an effect". With "bi-" (by) in front, it is "en bivirkning" (a side effect). To say a medicine has a side effect: "Medicinen har en bivirkning" (The medicine has a side effect).

sentence.da: Den nye lov fik en stor **virkning** på priserne.
sentence.en: The new law had a big effect on prices.

en virksomhed.explanation: "En virksomhed" means "a business". A common word partner is "privat" (private). For example, "en privat virksomhed" (a private business).

sentence.da: Hun driver en lille **virksomhed** med fem ansatte.
sentence.en: She runs a small business with five employees.

en virus.explanation: "En virus" means "a virus". To say you are sick because of one, use "at have" (to have): "Jeg har en virus" (I have a virus).

sentence.da: Min computer har fået en **virus** fra en e-mail.
sentence.en: My computer got a virus from an email.

en vision.explanation: "En vision" means "a vision", as in a plan for the future. To talk about eyesight, use "et syn" (eyesight): "Jeg har dårligt syn" (My eyesight is bad).

sentence.da: Firmaets **vision** er, at alle børn kan lære at læse.
sentence.en: The company's vision is that all children can learn to read.

en vissen blomst.explanation: "En vissen blomst" means "a withered flower". It comes from the verb "at visne" (to wither). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "vissen": "et vissent blad" (a withered leaf).

sentence.da: Uden vand bliver en blomst til en **vissen blomst**.
sentence.en: Without water, a flower turns into a withered flower.

et vitamin.explanation: "Et vitamin" means "a vitamin". To name a vitamin, put the letter first: "C-vitamin" (vitamin C).

sentence.da: Hun tager et **vitamin** hver morgen.
sentence.en: She takes a vitamin every morning.

en vits.explanation: "En vits" means "a joke". The last line that makes people laugh is "en pointe" (a punchline). To say you did not get the joke: "Jeg forstod ikke pointen" (I did not get the point).

sentence.da: Hun fortæller en **vits**, og alle griner.
sentence.en: She tells a joke, and everyone laughs.

en vittighed.explanation: "En vittighed" means "a joke". It is built from "vittig" (witty) and the ending "-hed". To say someone tells a joke: "Han fortæller en vittighed" (He tells a joke).

sentence.da: Alle grinede af hans **vittighed**.
sentence.en: Everyone laughed at his joke.

en vogn.explanation: "En vogn" means "a wagon or cart". As the last part of a word, "vogn" is in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart). For example, "Jeg skubber indkøbsvognen" (I push the shopping cart).

sentence.da: Hesten trækker en tung **vogn** op ad bakken.
sentence.en: The horse pulls a heavy wagon up the hill.

en vokal.explanation: "En vokal" means "a vowel". Danish has nine vowel letters. For example, "a", "e", "i", "o", "u", "y", "æ", "ø" and "å".

sentence.da: Ordet bil har kun én **vokal**, nemlig i.
sentence.en: The word bil has only one vowel, namely i.

en voksen.explanation: "En voksen" means "an adult". The word comes from "at vokse" (to grow). To say a film is for adults, use "for voksne": "en film for voksne" (a film for adults).

sentence.da: Et barn bliver til en **voksen**.
sentence.en: A child becomes an adult.

en vorte.explanation: "En vorte" means "a wart". To say a doctor takes it off: "Lægen fjerner vorten" (The doctor removes the wart).

sentence.da: Jeg har fået en **vorte** på fingeren, men den gør ikke ondt.
sentence.en: I got a wart on my finger, but it does not hurt.

en vugge.explanation: "En vugge" means "a cradle". The matching verb is "at vugge" (to rock). To say you rock a baby: "Hun vugger barnet" (She rocks the baby).

sentence.da: Den lille baby sover i en **vugge** ved sengen.
sentence.en: The little baby sleeps in a cradle next to the bed.

en vuggestue.explanation: "En vuggestue" means "a nursery". It is built from "en vugge" (a cradle) and "en stue" (a room). In Denmark, children go there until about three years old, then to "en børnehave" (a kindergarten). For example, "Hun går i børnehave" (She goes to kindergarten).

sentence.da: Vores datter går i **vuggestue**, mens vi er på arbejde.
sentence.en: Our daughter goes to a nursery while we are at work.

en vulkan.explanation: "En vulkan" means "a volcano". To talk about an eruption, use "et vulkanudbrud" (a volcanic eruption): "Der var et vulkanudbrud på Island" (There was a volcanic eruption in Iceland).

sentence.da: Der kommer varm lava ud af en **vulkan**.
sentence.en: Hot lava comes out of a volcano.

en vurdering.explanation: "En vurdering" means "an assessment". It comes from the verb "at vurdere" (to assess). To give an estimate of what something is worth: "Vurderingen af huset er to millioner kroner" (The assessment of the house is two million kroner).

sentence.da: Lægens **vurdering** er, at du skal hvile i en uge.
sentence.en: The doctor's assessment is that you should rest for a week.

en våbenhvile.explanation: "En våbenhvile" means "a ceasefire". It is built from "et våben" (a weapon) and "en hvile" (a rest).

sentence.da: Landene indgik en **våbenhvile**, og kampene stoppede.
sentence.en: The countries agreed to a ceasefire, and the fighting stopped.

en vædder.explanation: "En vædder" means "a ram". The star sign Aries is "Væderen" (the Ram). For example, "Væderen er et stjernetegn" (Aries is a star sign).

sentence.da: Den store **vædder** med krumme horn står på marken.
sentence.en: The big ram with curved horns is standing in the field.

en væg.explanation: "En væg" means "a wall", as in inside a room. For a wall outdoors, such as around a garden, use "en mur" (a wall of brick or stone): "Haven har en høj mur" (The garden has a tall wall).

sentence.da: Billedet hænger på en **væg**.
sentence.en: The picture hangs on a wall.

en vægt.explanation: "En vægt" means "a weight or a scale". To ask how heavy someone is: "Hvad er din vægt?" (What is your weight?) To talk about the machine you stand on to weigh yourself: "Vægten står på badeværelset" (The scale is in the bathroom).

sentence.da: Kufferten har en **vægt** på tyve kilo.
sentence.en: The suitcase has a weight of twenty kilos.

en vælger.explanation: "En vælger" means "a voter". It comes from "at vælge" (to choose). To ask who someone votes for, use "at stemme" (to vote): "Hvem stemmer du på?" (Who are you voting for?)

sentence.da: Hver **vælger** lægger sin stemme i urnen.
sentence.en: Each voter puts their vote in the ballot box.

en værdi.explanation: "En værdi" means "a value". To talk about what a person finds important, use the plural "værdier": "Vores værdier er ærlighed og frihed" (Our values are honesty and freedom).

sentence.da: Billedet har stor **værdi**, fordi det er meget gammelt.
sentence.en: The picture has great value because it is very old.

en vært.explanation: "En vært" means "a host", as in the person who has guests. It also means the host of a show. For example, "Hun er vært på et tv-program" (She is the host of a TV show). The word is part of "et værtshus" (a pub). For another example, "Vi mødes på værtshuset" (We meet at the pub).

sentence.da: Vores **vært** tog imod os ved døren.
sentence.en: Our host welcomed us at the door.

en værtinde.explanation: "En værtinde" means "a hostess". It is "en vært" (a host) plus the ending "-inde", which marks a woman, as in "en veninde" (a female friend).

sentence.da: Som **værtinde** skal hun sørge for, at gæsterne har det godt.
sentence.en: As hostess she must make sure the guests are doing well.

en værtindegave.explanation: "En værtindegave" means "a hostess gift". It is built from "en værtinde" (a hostess) and "en gave" (a gift). The part "gave" is also in "en fødselsdagsgave" (a birthday present). For example, "Jeg købte en fødselsdagsgave" (I bought a birthday present).

sentence.da: Jeg tog blomster med som **værtindegave**.
sentence.en: I brought flowers as a hostess gift.

en væske.explanation: "En væske" means "a liquid". To tell someone to drink plenty, use it for the fluids you drink: "Drik meget væske" (Drink a lot of fluids).

sentence.da: Vand er en **væske**, men is er fast.
sentence.en: Water is a liquid, but ice is solid.

et valg.explanation: "Et valg" means "a choice". To say a decision is up to someone: "Det er dit valg" (It is your choice). When you talk about voting for a parliament or a president, it means "an election": "Der er valg i år" (There is an election this year).

sentence.da: Du har et **valg**: te eller kaffe?
sentence.en: You have a choice: tea or coffee?

et vandfald.explanation: "Et vandfald" means "a waterfall". It is built from "vand" (water) and "et fald" (a fall). To talk about a drop in numbers, "et fald" is also used: "et fald i prisen" (a fall in the price).

sentence.da: Vandet falder ned fra et højt **vandfald**.
sentence.en: The water falls down from a tall waterfall.

et vandland.explanation: "Et vandland" means "a water park". It is built from "vand" (water) and "land" (land), so literally a land of water.

sentence.da: Vi tog børnene med til et **vandland**, hvor de kunne bade hele dagen.
sentence.en: We took the children to a water park where they could swim all day.

et vandrerhjem.explanation: "Et vandrerhjem" means "a hostel". It is built from "en vandrer" (a hiker) and "et hjem" (a home), so literally a hiker's home. The part "hjem" is also in "et plejehjem" (a nursing home). For example, "Min farmor bor på plejehjem" (My grandmother lives in a nursing home).

sentence.da: Vi bor billigt på et **vandrerhjem**.
sentence.en: We stay cheaply at a hostel.

et vareudvalg.explanation: "Et vareudvalg" means "a range of goods". It is built from "en vare" (an item) and "et udvalg" (a selection). The word "et udvalg" also means a committee. For example, "Kommunen har nedsat et udvalg" (The municipality has set up a committee).

sentence.da: Butikken har et stort **vareudvalg** og lave priser.
sentence.en: The store has a large range of goods and low prices.

et varsel.explanation: "Et varsel" means "a notice or warning". To talk about a weather warning: "Der er et varsel om storm i aften" (There is a storm warning tonight). To talk about advance notice at work: "Fagforeningen har givet varsel om strejke" (The union has given notice of a strike).

sentence.da: Vi fik kun en uges **varsel** om flytningen.
sentence.en: We got only a week's notice about the move.

et vaskemærke.explanation: "Et vaskemærke" means "a care label". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et mærke" (a label). The word "et mærke" also means a brand. For example, "et kendt mærke" (a famous brand).

sentence.da: Der står 30 grader på det lille **vaskemærke**.
sentence.en: It says 30 degrees on the little care label.

et vaskeri.explanation: "Et vaskeri" means "a laundromat". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and the ending "-eri", which names a place where the work is done, as in "et bageri" (a bakery). For example, "Vi køber brød på bageriet" (We buy bread at the bakery).

sentence.da: Jeg har ingen vaskemaskine og vasker på et **vaskeri**.
sentence.en: I have no washing machine and wash at a laundromat.

et vaskerum.explanation: "Et vaskerum" means "a laundry room". It is built from "vaske" (wash) and "et rum" (a room). The part "rum" is also in "et gæsterum" (a guest room). For example, "Du kan sove i gæsterummet" (You can sleep in the guest room).

sentence.da: Vi har et fælles **vaskerum** i kælderen.
sentence.en: We have a shared laundry room in the basement.

et vejskilt.explanation: "Et vejskilt" means "a road sign". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et skilt" (a sign). The word "et skilt" also works for any sign with writing. For example, "et skilt på døren" (a sign on the door).

sentence.da: På et **vejskilt** står der 50 kilometer til Aarhus.
sentence.en: On a road sign it says 50 kilometers to Aarhus.

et vendepunkt.explanation: "Et vendepunkt" means "a turning point". It is built from "at vende" (to turn) and "et punkt" (a point). To talk about a match, use it like this: "Det var et vendepunkt i kampen" (It was a turning point in the match).

sentence.da: Den dag blev et **vendepunkt** i hendes liv.
sentence.en: That day became a turning point in her life.

et venskab.explanation: "Et venskab" means "a friendship". It is built from "en ven" (a friend) and the ending "-skab". The same ending is in "et fællesskab" (a community). For example, "Vi har et godt fællesskab i klassen" (We have a good community in the class).

sentence.da: Deres **venskab** har holdt i mange år.
sentence.en: Their friendship has lasted for many years.

et venteværelse.explanation: "Et venteværelse" means "a waiting room". It is built from "at vente" (to wait) and "et værelse" (a room). The part "værelse" is also in "et soveværelse" (a bedroom). For example, "Vi har to soveværelser" (We have two bedrooms).

sentence.da: Vi venter på lægen i et **venteværelse**.
sentence.en: We wait for the doctor in a waiting room.

et verdenshav.explanation: "Et verdenshav" means "an ocean". It is built from "en verden" (a world) and "et hav" (a sea). To say you swim in the sea: "Jeg bader i havet" (I swim in the sea).

sentence.da: Atlanterhavet er et stort **verdenshav** mellem Europa og Amerika.
sentence.en: The Atlantic is a big ocean between Europe and America.

et vers.explanation: "Et vers" means "a verse". When it means poetry in general, it has no article: "Han skriver vers" (He writes poetry).

sentence.da: Sangen har tre **vers**, og vi kan alle synge dem.
sentence.en: The song has three verses, and we can all sing them.

et videoopkald.explanation: "Et videoopkald" means "a video call". It is built from "video" (video) and "et opkald" (a call). To talk about an ordinary phone call, use "et opkald" alone: "et opkald fra min mor" (a call from my mom).

sentence.da: Jeg ser min mormor i et **videoopkald** hver søndag.
sentence.en: I see my grandmother in a video call every Sunday.

et vidne.explanation: "Et vidne" means "a witness". To say you saw something happen, use "at være vidne til" (to witness): "Jeg var vidne til ulykken" (I witnessed the accident). A witness is a person, but "et bevis" (a piece of evidence) is a thing. For example, "Billedet er et bevis" (The photo is evidence).

sentence.da: Et **vidne** så bilen køre væk.
sentence.en: A witness saw the car drive away.

et vidnesbyrd.explanation: "Et vidnesbyrd" means "a testimony or evidence". To name what the evidence proves, use "om" (of): "et vidnesbyrd om hendes mod" (evidence of her courage). For what a person tells the police or a court, use "et vidneudsagn" (a witness statement): "Politiet har hørt hans vidneudsagn" (The police have heard his witness statement).

sentence.da: Den gamle kirke er et **vidnesbyrd** om byens historie.
sentence.en: The old church is evidence of the town's history.

et vidneudsagn.explanation: "Et vidneudsagn" means "a testimony". It is built from "et vidne" (a witness) and "et udsagn" (a statement). To talk about what someone said, use "et udsagn" alone: "Hans udsagn var forkert" (His statement was wrong).

sentence.da: Politiet har brug for dit **vidneudsagn** om ulykken.
sentence.en: The police need your testimony about the accident.

et vilkår.explanation: "Et vilkår" means "a term", as in an agreement. To tell someone to read the conditions of a contract: "Læs vilkårene først" (Read the terms first). When you talk about the circumstances someone works under, use it in the same way: "Det er svære vilkår at arbejde under" (These are difficult circumstances to work under).

sentence.da: Et **vilkår** i kontrakten er, at du møder til tiden.
sentence.en: One term in the contract is that you show up on time.

et vindue.explanation: "Et vindue" means "a window". To talk about a window on a computer screen, the same word is used: "åbn et nyt vindue" (open a new window).

sentence.da: Solen skinner ind gennem et **vindue**.
sentence.en: The sun shines in through a window.

et vinglas.explanation: "Et vinglas" means "a wine glass". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "et glas" (a glass). The word "glas" is also the material. For example, "en flaske af glas" (a bottle made of glass).

sentence.da: Hun hælder rødvin i et **vinglas**.
sentence.en: She pours red wine into a wine glass.

et visitkort.explanation: "Et visitkort" means "a business card". The part "kort" (card) is also in "et kreditkort" (a credit card). For example, "Jeg betaler med kreditkort" (I pay with a credit card).

sentence.da: Han gav mig sit **visitkort**, så jeg kunne ringe til ham.
sentence.en: He gave me his business card so that I could call him.

et viskelæder.explanation: "Et viskelæder" means "an eraser". It is built from "at viske" (to wipe) and "et læder" (leather). The word "læder" is also the material itself. For example, "en jakke af læder" (a jacket made of leather).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **viskelæder**, når jeg skriver forkert.
sentence.en: I use an eraser when I write something wrong.

et viskestykke.explanation: "Et viskestykke" means "a dish towel". It is built from "at viske" (to wipe) and "et stykke" (a piece). The word "et stykke" also works for a piece of food. For example, "et stykke kage" (a piece of cake).

sentence.da: Jeg tørrer tallerkenerne af med et **viskestykke**.
sentence.en: I dry the plates with a dish towel.

et visum.explanation: "Et visum" means "a visa". To say you have applied for one, use "at søge om" (to apply for): "Jeg har søgt om visum" (I have applied for a visa).

sentence.da: Du skal have et **visum** til Kina.
sentence.en: You need a visa for China.

et våben.explanation: "Et våben" means "a weapon". To use the word for something that is not physical: "Humor er et våben" (Humor is a weapon).

sentence.da: En kniv eller en pistol er et **våben**.
sentence.en: A knife or a pistol is a weapon.

et vådområde.explanation: "Et vådområde" means "a wetland". It is built from "våd" (wet) and "et område" (an area). The second part is also a word by itself. For example, "Området er lukket" (The area is closed).

sentence.da: I et **vådområde** er jorden våd det meste af året.
sentence.en: In a wetland, the ground is wet most of the year.

et væddemål.explanation: "Et væddemål" means "a bet". To say you bet on something, use the verb "at vædde" (to bet): "Jeg vil vædde på, at han kommer for sent" (I bet he will be late).

sentence.da: De lavede et **væddemål** om, hvem der vinder kampen.
sentence.en: They made a bet about who will win the match.

et vækkeur.explanation: "Et vækkeur" means "an alarm clock". It is built from "at vække" (to wake someone) and "et ur" (a clock). To ask someone to wake you: "Kan du vække mig i morgen?" (Can you wake me tomorrow?)

sentence.da: Jeg stiller mit **vækkeur** på seks.
sentence.en: I set my alarm clock to six.

et værelse.explanation: "Et værelse" means "a room", as in a room in a home or hotel. For room in the sense of free space, use "plads" (space): "Der er plads" (There is room).

sentence.da: Jeg har booket et **værelse** til to nætter.
sentence.en: I have booked a room for two nights.

et værk.explanation: "Et værk" means "a work", as in a work of art. For example, "Det er et af hans bedste værker" (It is one of his best works). To talk about a factory-like place, it is also the last part of words such as "et stålværk" (a steel mill): "Han arbejder på et stålværk" (He works at a steel mill).

sentence.da: Dette **værk** er malet af en kendt kunstner.
sentence.en: This work was painted by a famous artist.

et værksted.explanation: "Et værksted" means "a workshop or a garage". It is built from "et værk" (a work) and "et sted" (a place). For a garage where you park, use "en garage" (a garage): "Bilen står i garagen" (The car is in the garage).

sentence.da: Bilen skal repareres på et **værksted**.
sentence.en: The car has to be repaired at a workshop.

et værktøj.explanation: "Et værktøj" means "a tool". When you talk about tools in general, leave out "et": "Jeg har værktøj i skuret" (I have tools in the shed).

sentence.da: En hammer er et nyttigt **værktøj**.
sentence.en: A hammer is a useful tool.

et værn.explanation: "Et værn" means "a defense". To talk about protection against harm: "et værn mod kriminalitet" (a safeguard against crime). To name a part of the armed forces: "Hæren er et af værnene" (The army is one of the branches).

sentence.da: Loven er et **værn** mod misbrug af magt.
sentence.en: The law is a safeguard against abuse of power.

et værtshus.explanation: "Et værtshus" means "a pub". It is built from "en vært" (a host or landlord) and "et hus" (a house). The second part is also a word by itself. For example, "Vi bor i et stort hus" (We live in a big house).

sentence.da: På et **værtshus** kan man drikke øl og snakke med andre.
sentence.en: In a pub, you can drink beer and talk to others.

et væsen.explanation: "Et væsen" means "a creature or being". To talk about a person's nature, it means "manner": "Hun har et roligt væsen" (She has a calm manner).
