sentence.da: I eventyret bor der et **væsen** med vinger i skoven.
sentence.en: In the fairy tale, a creature with wings lives in the forest.

et væv.explanation: "Et væv" means "a tissue". It comes from the verb "at væve" (to weave). The same word is the last part of "et spindelvæv" (a spider web). For example, "Der hænger et spindelvæv i hjørnet" (A spider web hangs in the corner).

sentence.da: Kroppen består af mange slags **væv**, som alle har hver sin opgave.
sentence.en: The body is made of many kinds of tissue, which each have their own job.

vand.explanation: "Vand" means "water". It has no article when you talk about water in general. For example, "Jeg drikker vand" (I drink water). To order a drink, use "et glas" (a glass): "Et glas vand, tak" (A glass of water, please).

sentence.da: Fisk lever i **vand**.
sentence.en: Fish live in water.

vanilje.explanation: "Vanilje" means "vanilla". It is the first part of food words such as "vaniljeis" (vanilla ice cream). For example, "Jeg vil have en kugle vaniljeis" (I would like a scoop of vanilla ice cream).

sentence.da: Kagen smager af **vanilje**.
sentence.en: The cake tastes of vanilla.

vanskelig.explanation: "Vanskelig" means "difficult". A word with the same meaning is "svær" (hard). For example, "Opgaven er svær" (The task is hard). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "vanskelig": "et vanskeligt spørgsmål" (a difficult question).

sentence.da: Eksamen var **vanskelig**, men jeg bestod.
sentence.en: The exam was difficult, but I passed.

vant til.explanation: "Vant til" means "used to", as in being accustomed to something: "Jeg er vant til kulden" (I am used to the cold). For a past habit, use "plejede at" (used to): "Jeg plejede at bo i Aarhus" (I used to live in Aarhus).

forms.da: Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op.
forms.en: I am used to getting up early.

forms.da: Han er vant til hårdt arbejde.
forms.en: He is used to hard work.
We are used to the rain.

sentence.da: Jeg er **vant til** at cykle hver dag.
sentence.en: I am used to biking every day.

vanvid.explanation: "Et vanvid" means "a madness". To say an idea is reckless: "Det er vanvid at køre så hurtigt" (It is madness to drive that fast).

sentence.da: Støjen driver mig til **vanvid**.
sentence.en: The noise drives me mad.

vanvittig.explanation: "Vanvittig" means "crazy". To describe an idea: "en vanvittig idé" (a crazy idea). Before another describing word it means "extremely". For example, "Det er vanvittigt dyrt" (It is insanely expensive).

sentence.da: Det er en **vanvittig** idé, men jeg kan lide den.
sentence.en: It is a crazy idea, but I like it.

varetægt.explanation: "En varetægt" means "custody", as in "i politiets varetægt" (in police custody). For custody of a child, use "forældremyndighed" (parental custody) instead: "Hun har forældremyndigheden over børnene" (She has custody of the children).

sentence.da: Manden blev holdt i politiets **varetægt** natten over.
sentence.en: The man was held in police custody overnight.

varig.explanation: "Varig" means "lasting". It comes from the verb "at vare" (to last). When the thing takes "et", add "t" to "varig": "et varigt mén" (a lasting injury).

sentence.da: Vi søger en **varig** løsning på problemet.
sentence.en: We are looking for a lasting solution to the problem.

varm.explanation: "Varm" means "warm". To say a drink or food is hot, the same word is used: "varm kaffe" (hot coffee). When the thing takes "et", add "t": "et varmt hus" (a warm house).

sentence.da: Kaffen er **varm**, og isen er kold.
sentence.en: The coffee is hot and the ice cream is cold.

varme.explanation: "En varme" means "heat or warmth". To heat something up, use the verb "at varme" (to heat): "Jeg varmer suppen" (I am heating the soup). When it describes more than one thing, "varme" means "warm": "varme dage" (warm days).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tåle **varme**.
sentence.en: I can't stand heat.

varsom.explanation: "Varsom" means "cautious". To say what you are careful with, add "med" (with): "at være varsom med sine ord" (to choose your words with care).

sentence.da: Vær **varsom**, fordi bogen er gammel og skrøbelig.
sentence.en: Be cautious because the book is old and fragile.

vaskepulver.explanation: "Vaskepulver" means "laundry detergent". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "et pulver" (a powder). The word for any kind of detergent, powder or liquid, is "et vaskemiddel" (a detergent). For example, "Vaskemidlet står på hylden" (The detergent is on the shelf).

sentence.da: Jeg putter **vaskepulver** i vaskemaskinen.
sentence.en: I put laundry detergent in the washing machine.

vasketøj.explanation: "Vasketøj" means "laundry". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "tøj" (clothes). To say you have a lot of laundry, use no article before "vasketøj": "Jeg har meget vasketøj" (I have a lot of laundry).

sentence.da: Jeg sorterer **vasketøj** i hvidt og farvet.
sentence.en: I sort laundry into white and colored.

ved.explanation: "Ved" means "by". To say where someone sits next to something: "Han sidder ved vinduet" (He sits by the window). When you talk about a table or desk where someone sits or works, it means "at": "Vi sidder ved bordet" (We sit at the table). The same spelling is also a form of "at vide" (to know). For example, "Jeg ved det" (I know it).

sentence.da: Vi mødes **ved** stationen.
sentence.en: We are meeting at the station.

ved siden af.explanation: "Ved siden af" means "next to". It is built from "ved" (by), "siden" (the side) and "af" (of), so literally by the side of. To say you do something in addition to a job: "Jeg læser ved siden af mit arbejde" (I study alongside my job).

sentence.da: Banken ligger **ved siden af** posthuset.
sentence.en: The bank is next to the post office.

vedholdenhed.explanation: "En vedholdenhed" means "a persistence". To say that a task needs it: "Det kræver vedholdenhed at skrive en bog" (It takes persistence to write a book). For the strength of your body, use "udholdenhed" (stamina): "Maratonløbere har stor udholdenhed" (Marathon runners have great stamina).

sentence.da: Med **vedholdenhed** og tid kan man lære næsten alt.
sentence.en: With persistence and time you can learn almost anything.

vedkommende.explanation: "Vedkommende" means "the person". To talk about a person without saying "han" (he) or "hun" (she): "Vedkommende har ikke svaret" (The person has not answered).

forms.en: The person is not at home.

sentence.da: **Vedkommende** har ringet tre gange, men siger ikke sit navn.
sentence.en: The person has called three times, but does not say their name.

vedligeholdelse.explanation: "Vedligeholdelse" means "maintenance". To talk about fixing something that is already broken, use "en reparation" (a repair): "Bilen skal til reparation" (The car needs repair).

sentence.da: Ejerforeningen betaler for **vedligeholdelse** af trapper og gård.
sentence.en: The owners' association pays for maintenance of the stairs and the yard.

vedrørende.explanation: "Vedrørende" means "regarding". To name the subject of a letter or email, write it first: "Vedrørende din bestilling" (Regarding your order). It is shortened to "vedr." in writing.

sentence.da: Jeg skriver **vedrørende** din ansøgning om jobbet.
sentence.en: I am writing concerning your application for the job.

vedvarende.explanation: "Vedvarende" means "persistent". It comes from "at vare" (to last). In "vedvarende energi" it means "renewable".

sentence.da: Hun har **vedvarende** smerter i ryggen efter ulykken.
sentence.en: She has persistent pain in her back after the accident.

vedvarende energi.explanation: "Vedvarende energi" means "renewable energy". It is "vedvarende" (lasting) and "energi" (energy), so literally lasting energy.

sentence.da: Danmark får meget **vedvarende energi** fra vindmøller.
sentence.en: Denmark gets a lot of renewable energy from wind turbines.

vegansk.explanation: "Vegansk" means "vegan". To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en veganer" (a vegan): "Min søster er veganer" (My sister is a vegan).

sentence.da: Jeg bager en **vegansk** kage uden æg og smør.
sentence.en: I am baking a vegan cake without eggs or butter.

vegetarisk.explanation: "Vegetarisk" means "vegetarian". To ask a restaurant for food without meat: "Har I noget vegetarisk?" (Do you have anything vegetarian?) To talk about a person who eats this way, use "en vegetar" (a vegetarian): "Min bror er vegetar" (My brother is a vegetarian).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser ikke kød. En **vegetarisk** ret, tak.
sentence.en: I don't eat meat. A vegetarian dish, please.

vejarbejde.explanation: "Vejarbejde" means "roadworks". It is built from "en vej" (a road) and "et arbejde" (a job). To warn about a road: "Der er vejarbejde på motorvejen" (There are roadworks on the highway).

sentence.da: Vejen er lukket på grund af **vejarbejde**.
sentence.en: The road is closed because of roadworks.

vejr.explanation: "Vejr" means "weather". To ask what it is like outside: "Hvordan er vejret?" (How is the weather?) The same word is also in "at trække vejret" (to breathe), where it means "the breath": "Jeg kan ikke trække vejret" (I cannot breathe).

sentence.da: Regn og vind er dårligt **vejr**.
sentence.en: Rain and wind are bad weather.

vejrtrækning.explanation: "En vejrtrækning" means "a breath or breathing". It is built on "at trække vejret" (to take a breath), where "vejret" means "the breath" here, not the weather. To say you hold your breath: "Jeg holder vejret" (I am holding my breath).

sentence.da: Din **vejrtrækning** bliver hurtigere, når du løber.
sentence.en: Your breathing gets faster when you run.

vel.explanation: "Vel" means "I suppose". To say you guess that something is fine: "Det er vel i orden" (I suppose that is fine). To ask a question where you expect the answer no: "Han er vel ikke gået?" (He has not left, has he?)

forms.en: You are not sick, are you?
He is probably home by now.
I suppose it does not cost much.

sentence.da: Du kommer **vel** i morgen?
sentence.en: You are coming tomorrow, right?

velbegrundet.explanation: "Velbegrundet" means "well-founded". It is built from "vel" (well) and "begrundet" (given reasons for).

sentence.da: Hans kritik er **velbegrundet**, fordi han kender sagen godt.
sentence.en: His criticism is well-founded because he knows the case well.

velbekomme.explanation: "Velbekomme" means "Enjoy! or You're welcome!". When you put food in front of someone, say it: "Velbekomme!" (Enjoy!) When someone thanks you for a meal, say it back: "Tak for en dejlig middag." "Velbekomme." (Thanks for a lovely dinner. You're welcome.) For other thanks, say "selv tak" (you're welcome): "Tak for hjælpen." "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. You're welcome.)

forms.en: Thanks for the meal. You're welcome.

sentence.da: Her er suppen. **Velbekomme**!
sentence.en: Here is the soup. Enjoy!

veldrevet.explanation: "Veldrevet" means "well-run". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at drive" (to run), as in "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop). For a place that looks neat and cared for, use "velholdt" (well-kept): "et velholdt hus" (a well-kept house).

sentence.da: Bageriet er **veldrevet**, og der er altid kunder i butikken.
sentence.en: The bakery is well-run, and there are always customers in the store.

velfortjent.explanation: "Velfortjent" means "well-deserved". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at fortjene" (to deserve). The opposite is "ufortjent" (undeserved). For example, "Det var en ufortjent sejr" (It was an undeserved win).

forms.en: a well-deserved pat on the back

sentence.da: Efter en hård uge får hun en **velfortjent** pause.
sentence.en: After a hard week she gets a well-deserved break.

velfærd.explanation: "Velfærd" means "welfare". In Denmark it especially means public services paid for by taxes, such as health care, schools and care for the old. A country that provides them is "en velfærdsstat" (a welfare state). For example, "Danmark er en velfærdsstat" (Denmark is a welfare state).

sentence.da: Danmark bruger mange penge på **velfærd**, fordi skatten er høj.
sentence.en: Denmark spends a lot of money on welfare because taxes are high.

velfærdssamfundet.explanation: "Et velfærdssamfund" means "a welfare society". It is built from "velfærd" (welfare) and "et samfund" (a society). In Denmark, taxes pay for things such as schools and health care.

sentence.da: I **velfærdssamfundet** er sygehuse og skoler gratis for alle.
sentence.en: In the welfare society, hospitals and schools are free for everyone.

velgørenhed.explanation: "Velgørenhed" means "charity". For a charity as an organization, use "en velgørenhedsorganisation" (a charity organization): "Jeg giver penge til en velgørenhedsorganisation" (I give money to a charity organization).

sentence.da: Alle pengene fra koncerten går til **velgørenhed**.
sentence.en: All the money from the concert goes to charity.

velhavende.explanation: "Velhavende" means "wealthy". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at have" (to have). A shorter word with the same meaning is "rig" (rich). For example, "Han er rig" (He is rich).

sentence.da: Hun er **velhavende**, fordi hun ejer flere huse.
sentence.en: She is wealthy because she owns several houses.

velholdt.explanation: "Velholdt" means "well-kept". It is built from "vel" (well) and "holdt" (kept). To describe a house in good condition: "Huset er meget velholdt" (The house is very well-kept). For a business that is managed well, use "veldrevet" (well-run): "en veldrevet butik" (a well-run shop).

sentence.da: Bilen er tyve år gammel, men meget **velholdt**.
sentence.en: The car is twenty years old, but very well-kept.

velkendt.explanation: "Velkendt" means "well-known". It is built from "vel" (well) and "kendt" (known). When you know a face or a tune well yourself, it means "familiar": "et velkendt ansigt" (a familiar face).

sentence.da: Tivoli er et **velkendt** sted, som mange turister besøger.
sentence.en: Tivoli is a well-known place that many tourists visit.

velklædt.explanation: "Velklædt" means "well-dressed". It is built from "vel" (well) and "klædt" (dressed), from "at klæde" (to dress). To say how someone looks: "Hun ser velklædt ud" (She looks well-dressed).

sentence.da: Han er **velklædt**, fordi han skal til et bryllup.
sentence.en: He is well-dressed because he is going to a wedding.

velkommen.explanation: "Velkommen" means "welcome". To welcome someone to a place, add "til" (to) before the place: "Velkommen til Danmark" (Welcome to Denmark). To answer "tak" (thanks), say "selv tak" (you're welcome): "Tak for hjælpen." "Selv tak." (Thanks for the help. You're welcome.)

sentence.da: **Velkommen** til vores hjem!
sentence.en: Welcome to our home!

vellykket.explanation: "Vellykket" means "successful". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at lykkes" (to succeed). To say an event or a trip turned out well: "Rejsen var vellykket" (The trip was successful). For a person or a company, use "succesfuld" (successful): "en succesfuld forretningsmand" (a successful businessman).

sentence.da: Festen var **vellykket**, og alle gik glade hjem.
sentence.en: The party was successful, and everyone went home happy.

velopdragen.explanation: "Velopdragen" means "well-behaved". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at opdrage" (to bring up). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et velopdraget barn" (a well-behaved child).

sentence.da: Min hund er **velopdragen** og går pænt i snor.
sentence.en: My dog is well-behaved and walks nicely on a leash.

velsmagende.explanation: "Velsmagende" means "tasty". It is built from "vel" (well) and "at smage" (to taste). To praise food: "Maden er velsmagende" (The food is tasty).

sentence.da: Suppen var **velsmagende**, fordi den var lavet af friske grøntsager.
sentence.en: The soup was tasty because it was made from fresh vegetables.

vemodig.explanation: "Vemodig" means "wistful". It comes from "vemod" (a soft, quiet sadness). To say how someone smiled, add "t": "Hun smilede vemodigt" (She smiled wistfully).

sentence.da: Det gør mig **vemodig** at se gamle billeder af os.
sentence.en: It makes me wistful to see old pictures of us.

venlig.explanation: "Venlig" means "kind". It comes from "en ven" (a friend). To end a letter or an email: "Venlig hilsen" (Kind regards).

sentence.da: Hun er **venlig** og smiler til mig.
sentence.en: She is friendly and smiles at me.

venlighed.explanation: "Venlighed" means "kindness". It comes from "venlig" (kind). To thank someone for being kind: "Tak for din venlighed" (Thank you for your kindness).

sentence.da: Vi mødte stor **venlighed** på rejsen.
sentence.en: We met great kindness on the trip.

venligst.explanation: "Venligst" means "please". It sounds formal. To politely ask someone to wait: "Vent venligst" (Please wait).

sentence.da: Husk **venligst** at lukke døren.
sentence.en: Please remember to close the door.

venstre.explanation: "Venstre" means "left", as in the opposite of right. To give directions: "Drej til venstre" (Turn left). "Venstre" is also the name of a Danish political party. For example, "Han stemmer på Venstre" (He votes for Venstre).

sentence.da: Tag den første vej til **venstre**.
sentence.en: Take the first road on the left.

vent lidt.explanation: "Vent lidt" means "wait a bit". It is "vent" (the command form of "at vente", to wait) and "lidt" (a bit). To make it more polite, add "tak" (thanks): "Vent lidt, tak" (Wait a bit, please).

sentence.da: Jeg leder efter min taske. **Vent lidt**!
sentence.en: I'm looking for my bag. Wait a bit!

vest.explanation: "Vest" means "west". To say where the wind comes from: "Vinden kommer fra vest" (The wind comes from the west). It is also part of "Vestjylland" (West Jutland), the western part of Jutland, the Danish mainland.

sentence.da: Solen går ned i **vest**.
sentence.en: The sun goes down in the west.

vestlig.explanation: "Vestlig" means "westerly". It is built from "vest" (west). To say a place is in the western part of a country, use "det vestlige" (the western part): "Esbjerg ligger i det vestlige Danmark" (Esbjerg is in western Denmark).

sentence.da: Vinden kommer fra en **vestlig** retning.
sentence.en: The wind comes from a westerly direction.

vestpå.explanation: "Vestpå" means "west", for moving toward the west. To say a plane changes direction: "Flyet drejer vestpå" (The plane turns west). To say where a place lies, use "vest for" (west of): "Esbjerg ligger vest for Odense" (Esbjerg is west of Odense).

sentence.da: Toget kører **vestpå** mod Esbjerg.
sentence.en: The train goes west toward Esbjerg.

vi.explanation: "Vi" means "we". To say what we do: "Vi bor her" (We live here). When you mean "us", use "os" instead: "Han ser os" (He sees us).

sentence.da: I dag spiser **vi** hjemme.
sentence.en: Today we eat at home.

vi ses.explanation: "Vi ses" means "see you". Literally, it is "we see each other". When you say goodbye to someone you will meet again, add the time: "Vi ses på fredag" (See you on Friday).

sentence.da: Jeg skal gå nu. **Vi ses** i morgen!
sentence.en: I have to go now. See you tomorrow!

vi snakkes.explanation: "Vi snakkes" means "talk to you later". To end a call when you expect to speak again: "Tak for hjælpen, vi snakkes!" (Thanks for the help, talk to you later!)

sentence.da: Jeg har travlt nu, men **vi snakkes**.
sentence.en: I'm busy now, but talk to you later.

vi tales ved.explanation: "Vi tales ved" means "talk soon". To end a call when you will speak again: "Jeg ringer i morgen, vi tales ved!" (I will call tomorrow, talk soon!) When you expect to meet in person, say "vi ses" (see you): "Vi ses på kontoret" (See you at the office).

sentence.da: Jeg ringer i aften. **Vi tales ved**!
sentence.en: I'll call tonight. Talk soon!

via.explanation: "Via" means "via". To say the route of a trip: "Vi kører via Odense" (We drive via Odense). To say how you contact someone: "Skriv til mig via mail" (Write to me via email).

sentence.da: Vi rejser **via** København til Aarhus.
sentence.en: We travel via Copenhagen to Aarhus.

viden.explanation: "Viden" means "knowledge". It comes from "at vide" (to know). To talk about knowledge in general, use it without an article: "Viden er magt" (Knowledge is power).

sentence.da: Hun har meget **viden** om historie.
sentence.en: She has a lot of knowledge about history.

videnskabelig.explanation: "Videnskabelig" means "scientific". It is built from "en videnskab" (a science), which comes from "viden" (knowledge). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et videnskabeligt forsøg" (a scientific experiment).

sentence.da: En **videnskabelig** undersøgelse bruger målinger til at finde svar.
sentence.en: A scientific study uses measurements to find answers.

vidtrækkende.explanation: "Vidtrækkende" means "far-reaching". To say a change will affect many things: "Det får vidtrækkende konsekvenser" (It will have far-reaching consequences).

sentence.da: Regeringens beslutning er **vidtrækkende**, og alle landets skoler bliver ramt.
sentence.en: The government's decision is far-reaching, and all the country's schools are affected.

vidunderlig.explanation: "Vidunderlig" means "wonderful". It is built on "et vidunder" (a wonder). When you talk about an event, add "t": "Det var vidunderligt!" (That was wonderful!)

sentence.da: Solnedgangen over havet var **vidunderlig**.
sentence.en: The sunset over the sea was wonderful.

vigtig.explanation: "Vigtig" means "important". To say who something matters to, add "for" (for): "Det er vigtigt for mig" (It is important to me). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et vigtigt møde" (an important meeting).

sentence.da: Søvn er **vigtig** for din krop.
sentence.en: Sleep is important for your body.

vikingetiden.explanation: "Vikingetiden" means "the Viking Age". It is built from "viking" (Viking) and "tiden" (the time). In Danish history, it is dated from about 800 to 1050. To say something happened then: "Skibene blev bygget i vikingetiden" (The ships were built in the Viking Age).

forms.en: the ships of the Viking Age

sentence.da: I **vikingetiden** sejlede mange danskere til England og Irland.
sentence.en: In the Viking Age, many Danes sailed to England and Ireland.

vild.explanation: "Vild" means "wild", as in an animal or plant that lives free. To talk about plants that grow free: "vilde blomster" (wild flowers). A different use: to say a party was amazing, say "Den fest var vild" (That party was amazing).

sentence.da: Hesten var **vild**, men nu er den rolig.
sentence.en: The horse was wild, but now it is calm.

vild med.explanation: "Vild med" means "crazy about". It comes after "er" (am/is/are). For example, "Jeg er vild med pizza" (I am crazy about pizza). When more than one person feels it, "vild" becomes "vilde": "De er vilde med sne" (They are crazy about snow).

sentence.da: Min søn er **vild med** fodbold.
sentence.en: My son is crazy about soccer.

vildt.explanation: "Vildt" means "wild". It is the form of "vild" (wild) used in front of a word that takes "et": "et vildt dyr" (a wild animal). A different use: to react to something amazing, say "Det var vildt!" (That was crazy!)

sentence.da: En ræv er et **vildt** dyr.
sentence.en: A fox is a wild animal.

villig.explanation: "Villig" means "willing". To say what someone is willing to do, add "til at" (to) before the verb: "Hun er villig til at hjælpe" (She is willing to help). In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et villigt barn" (a willing child).

sentence.da: Hun er **villig** til at vente lidt.
sentence.en: She is willing to wait a little.

villighed.explanation: "Villighed" means "willingness". It is built from "villig" (willing). To thank someone for being ready to help: "Tak for din villighed" (Thank you for your willingness).

sentence.da: Hendes **villighed** til at hjælpe gjorde os alle glade.
sentence.en: Her willingness to help made us all glad.

vind.explanation: "Vind" means "wind". To say it is windy, use "at blæse" (to blow): "Det blæser i dag" (It is windy today).

sentence.da: Sejlbåden bruger **vind** til at sejle.
sentence.en: The sailboat uses wind to sail.

vindende.explanation: "Vindende" means "winning". It comes from "at vinde" (to win). A different use: a smile that charms people is "et vindende smil" (a winning smile).

sentence.da: Det **vindende** hold fik en pokal og tusind kroner.
sentence.en: The winning team got a trophy and a thousand kroner.

vindenergi.explanation: "Vindenergi" means "wind power". It is built from "vind" (wind) and "energi" (energy). To say a country makes wind power: "Danmark producerer meget vindenergi" (Denmark produces a lot of wind power).

sentence.da: **Vindenergi** er ren energi, fordi den ikke forurener luften.
sentence.en: Wind power is clean energy because it does not pollute the air.

vinterbadning.explanation: "Vinterbadning" means "winter swimming". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "badning" (bathing), from "at bade" (to bathe). In Denmark, many people swim in the sea in winter and meet in a club. To say you do it: "Jeg går til vinterbadning hver søndag" (I go winter swimming every Sunday).

sentence.da: Efter **vinterbadning** i det kolde hav varmer vi os i saunaen.
sentence.en: After winter swimming in the cold sea, we warm up in the sauna.

viral.explanation: "Viral" means "viral". To say a post spread fast online: "Opslaget blev viralt" (The post went viral). A different use: to say a disease is caused by a virus: "en viral infektion" (a viral infection).

sentence.da: Videoen blev **viral**, og millioner af mennesker så den.
sentence.en: The video went viral, and millions of people saw it.

virkelig.explanation: "Virkelig" means "really". To make a word stronger: "virkelig dejlig" (really lovely). To react to surprising news: "Virkelig?" (Really?)

sentence.da: Maden er **virkelig** god.
sentence.en: The food is really good.

visdom.explanation: "Visdom" means "wisdom". It is the first part of "en visdomstand" (a wisdom tooth) and "et visdomsord" (a word of wisdom).

sentence.da: **Visdom** kommer med alderen, ikke fra bøger.
sentence.en: Wisdom comes with age, not from books.

visse.explanation: "Visse" means "certain". To talk about one certain thing, use "en vis" or "et vist": "en vis tid" (a certain time). To say you are sure, use "sikker" (sure): "Jeg er sikker" (I am sure).

sentence.da: **Visse** mennesker elsker kulde, men ikke alle.
sentence.en: Certain people love the cold, but not everyone.

vist.explanation: "Vist" means "I think". To say you believe something but are not sure, put it after the verb: "Han er vist syg" (I think he is sick). A different use: "vist" is also the word for "shown", as in "Filmen blev vist i går" (The film was shown yesterday).

forms.en: I do not think we have milk

sentence.da: Han er **vist** hjemme nu.
sentence.en: I think he is home now.

vistnok.explanation: "Vistnok" means "I believe". It is built from "vist" (I think) and "nok" (probably). To pass on something you heard but are not sure of: "Hun er vistnok hjemme" (She is home, I believe).

forms.en: He is coming tomorrow, I believe.

sentence.da: Han er **vistnok** flyttet til Aarhus, men jeg er ikke sikker.
sentence.en: He has apparently moved to Aarhus, but I am not sure.

vittig.explanation: "Vittig" means "witty". A joke is "en vittighed". For example, "Han fortæller en vittighed" (He tells a joke). Do not mix it up with "vigtig" (important). For another example, "Det er vigtigt" (It is important).

sentence.da: Han er **vittig**, fordi han altid finder et hurtigt, sjovt svar.
sentence.en: He is witty, because he always finds a quick, funny answer.

voksen.explanation: "Voksen" means "grown-up". It comes from "at vokse" (to grow). As a noun, "en voksen" is a grown-up. For example, "børn og voksne" (children and grown-ups).

sentence.da: Når man er **voksen**, arbejder man.
sentence.en: When you are an adult, you work.

vold.explanation: "Vold" means "violence". To say someone uses violence: "at bruge vold" (to use violence). To say it is forbidden: "Vold i hjemmet er forbudt" (Violence in the home is forbidden).

sentence.da: **Vold** er, når man med vilje gør andre fysisk ondt.
sentence.en: Violence is when you deliberately physically hurt others.

voldelig.explanation: "Voldelig" means "violent", as in hurting people. It is built from "vold" (violence). For a storm or a pain with great force, use "voldsom" (violent): "en voldsom storm" (a violent storm).

sentence.da: Han blev dømt, fordi han var **voldelig** over for sin nabo.
sentence.en: He was convicted because he was violent toward his neighbor.

voldsom.explanation: "Voldsom" means "violent", as in great force. It is built from "vold" (violence). To describe a person who hurts others, use "voldelig" (violent): "Han er voldelig" (He is violent).

sentence.da: En **voldsom** storm rev tagene af husene.
sentence.en: A violent storm tore the roofs off the houses.

volleyball.explanation: "Volleyball" means "volleyball". To say you play it, use "at spille" (to play): "Hun spiller volleyball hver tirsdag" (She plays volleyball every Tuesday). It starts longer words. For example, "en volleyballkamp" (a volleyball match).

sentence.da: Vi spiller **volleyball** på stranden om sommeren.
sentence.en: We play volleyball on the beach in the summer.

vores.explanation: "Vores" means "our". It does not change, whatever follows. For example, "vores børn" (our children).

sentence.da: **Vores** hus er meget stort.
sentence.en: Our house is very big.

vred.explanation: "Vred" means "angry". To name who you are angry at, use "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på dig" (I am angry at you). When more than one person is angry, "vred" becomes "vrede": "De er vrede på mig" (They are angry at me).

sentence.da: Han er meget **vred** på mig.
sentence.en: He is very angry at me.

vred på.explanation: "Vred på" means "angry at". To name who you are angry at, put the person after "på" (at): "Jeg er vred på ham" (I am angry at him). When more than one person is angry, "vred" becomes "vrede": "Vi er vrede på chefen" (We are angry at the boss).

forms.da: Jeg er vred på mig selv.

forms.en: They are angry at each other.

sentence.da: Hun er **vred på** sin bror, fordi han løj.
sentence.en: She is angry at her brother because he lied.

vrede.explanation: "Vrede" means "anger". To say someone feels anger: "Hun følte vrede, da han løj" (She felt anger when he lied). The same spelling is also the plural of "vred" (angry). For example, "De er vrede" (They are angry).

sentence.da: Folk følte **vrede**, fordi regeringen havde brudt sit løfte.
sentence.en: People felt anger because the government had broken its promise.

vrøvl.explanation: "Vrøvl" means "nonsense". It is the noun for "at vrøvle" (to talk nonsense). For example, "Hold op med at vrøvle!" (Stop talking nonsense!) It is blunt, so with someone you do not know well, say "Jeg er ikke enig" (I do not agree) instead.

sentence.da: Det er noget **vrøvl**, og jeg tror ikke på det.
sentence.en: That is nonsense, and I do not believe it.

våd.explanation: "Våd" means "wet". In front of a word that takes "et", add "t": "et vådt håndklæde" (a wet towel). With more than one thing, add "e": "våde hunde" (wet dogs).

sentence.da: Hunden er helt **våd** af regn.
sentence.en: The dog is completely wet from rain.

vågen.explanation: "Vågen" means "awake". To ask if someone is awake: "Er du vågen?" (Are you awake?) Do not mix it up with "at vågne" (to wake up): "Jeg vågnede klokken syv" (I woke up at seven).

sentence.da: Jeg er **vågen** hele natten.
sentence.en: I am awake all night.

væk.explanation: "Væk" means "gone". To say you cannot find something: "Min nøgle er væk" (My key is gone). A different use: to say someone moves away, use "away": "Hun løber væk" (She runs away). "Gå væk!" (Go away!) is blunt.

sentence.da: Min taske er **væk**!
sentence.en: My bag is gone!

vækst.explanation: "Vækst" means "growth". It is the noun for the verb "at vokse" (to grow). For example, "Planterne vokser hurtigt" (The plants are growing fast). To talk about a country's economy: "økonomisk vækst" (economic growth).

sentence.da: Virksomheden har haft stor **vækst** og ansætter nu flere folk.
sentence.en: The company has had big growth and is now hiring more people.

vældig.explanation: "Vældig" means "very". To make a word stronger: "vældig glad" (very happy).

sentence.da: Maden var **vældig** god.
sentence.en: The food was very good.

værd.explanation: "Værd" means "worth". To say how much something is worth, put "værd" after the amount: "Cyklen er tusind kroner værd" (The bike is worth a thousand kroner). To say something is worth doing, add "at" (to) before the verb: "værd at prøve" (worth trying).

forms.en: It is not worth the money.

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel er ikke mange penge **værd**.
sentence.en: The old bike is not worth much money.

værdifuld.explanation: "Værdifuld" means "valuable". It is built from "værdi" (value) and "fuld" (full). The same ending is in "smertefuld" (painful, literally "full of pain").

sentence.da: Den gamle ring er meget **værdifuld**.
sentence.en: The old ring is very valuable.

værdig.explanation: "Værdig" means "worthy". To name what the person deserves, add "til" (of): "værdig til respekt" (worthy of respect). A different meaning is "dignified". For example, "et værdigt svar" (a dignified answer).

sentence.da: Hun er en **værdig** vinder, fordi hun har trænet i årevis.
sentence.en: She is a worthy winner because she has trained for years.

værdighed.explanation: "Værdighed" means "dignity". It is built from "værdig" (worthy). To say someone stays calm and proud: "Hun gik med værdighed" (She walked with dignity).

sentence.da: Han tabte sagen, men forlod retten med **værdighed**.
sentence.en: He lost the case, but left the court with dignity.

værdiløs.explanation: "Værdiløs" means "worthless". It is built from "værdi" (value) and "løs" (without). The ending "løs" is also in "hjælpeløs" (helpless) and "søvnløs" (sleepless).

sentence.da: Aktien er **værdiløs**, fordi firmaet er gået konkurs.
sentence.en: The share is worthless because the company has gone bankrupt.

værdsat.explanation: "Værdsat" means "appreciated". It comes from "at værdsætte" (to appreciate). To thank a coworker: "Du er en værdsat kollega" (You are an appreciated colleague).

sentence.da: Hun føler sig **værdsat**, fordi chefen takker hende hver uge.
sentence.en: She feels appreciated because her boss thanks her every week.

værre.explanation: "Værre" means "worse". It is the form of "dårlig" (bad) for comparing two things. For example, "Maden er værre her end hjemme" (The food is worse here than at home). To say a situation is quite bad: "et værre rod" (quite a mess).

sentence.da: I dag er det **værre** end i går.
sentence.en: Today it is worse than yesterday.

værsgo.explanation: "Værsgo" means "here you go". To invite someone to do something, it means "go ahead". It is short for "vær så god" (be so good).

forms.en: Here you go, here is your coffee.

sentence.da: Må jeg låne din pen? **Værsgo**!
sentence.en: May I borrow your pen? Go ahead!

værst.explanation: "Værst" means "worst". It is the form of "dårlig" (bad) for the worst of all. For example, "Det værste er, at vi mistede bussen" (The worst thing is that we missed the bus). For two things, use "værre" (worse): "Det er værre end i går" (It is worse than yesterday).

sentence.da: Vejret er **værst** i januar.
sentence.en: The weather is the worst in January.

væsentlig.explanation: "Væsentlig" means "significant". To say it does not matter, put "ikke" (not) before it: "Det er ikke væsentligt, hvem der vinder" (It is not important who wins). For a person, say "vigtig" (important): "en vigtig person" (an important person).

sentence.da: Der er en **væsentlig** forskel på de to tilbud.
sentence.en: There is a significant difference between the two offers.
